Keep pending until the router is running, then (a) if FreeLLMAPI can declare a one-model chain per pinned id, else (b).

SR-026Coordinator resumes headlessre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator shall resume headless with stdin closed, never blocking on a prompt: a worker resumes from its explicit claimed assignment plus the committed trailer evidence on its branch, and the integrator derives claim and queue state from trunk history alone — the generated status surface never a session input.

Rationale

Realizes SN-006 and the dissolved edge expectation that an unattended run never blocks on a prompt, at launch or mid-run. The acceptance is deliberately narrower than it once was: it had carried two obligations the shall never stated - transient-limit backoff and stall abort - and an acceptance cell cannot mint a requirement. Both were MINTED rather than deleted, because each describes live behaviour worth keeping: SR-171 and SR-172. An unattended run blocked on a prompt is indistinguishable from a hung one and holds its lane until an operator notices. Keeping a separate serial resume path beside the dispatcher was rejected: two authorities over one decision drift, and the divergence surfaces as a run that resumes differently depending on how it was started.

The scheduling front end a plain agent_loop.py launch runs, serial at lanes=1 (the lanes dial admits more lanes at once; each lane's mechanics are LLR-150's): each cycle re-derives the ready frontier (schedule.frontier), stops claiming under the tracked pause (a parked or finished lane still resumes and merges, and the run exits 8 once nothing is in flight), refuses on a dirty trunk at the cycle top while no lane is live (a change confined to agent_common.OWNER_ONLY_PATHS,agent_common.OPERATOR_ONLY_PATHS, the owner'soperator's scratchpad, is not dirt), resumes a parked claimed branch else claims the next queued WI in build order (integrate.claim, branch name check-ref-format-validated), launches one worker session on the claimed branch's worktree (agent_loop.py --worktree --wi with the session dials forwarded), merges each finished branch through the serial merge slot (integrate.integrate) counting the WIs merged, and stops loudly on any composed refusal once the live lanes drain - a stall aborts, an empty frontier drains to exit 0. A NEEDS-HUMANNEEDS-OPERATOR worker does not stop the run: its lane hands back (the WI closes partial and merges) and the run drives on; an active/ directory with no branch ref is residue, not a refusal. A parked claimed branch whose claimed row reads blocked in the shared schedule is left out of resume: it launches no worker, keeps its claim, and the next ready row is claimed; the excluded lane does not count as a stall. A parked lane whose claimed row reads anything else resumes as before. The session-config preflight applies only when work needs a worker. Never pushes.

SR-031Declared-policy readers agreere-accept owed

Requirement

Every delivered enforcer of a declared policy dial shall read the same value for that dial as every other enforcer — one parse, one answer, across the hooks, the loop and the checkers alike.

Rationale

Realizes SN-028's one readable policy home. A policy answer calculated more than once can diverge across enforcers, leaving the operator unable to know which value governs; one parse gives every enforcer the same answer. SR-137 owns whether a declaration is ambiguous or invalid, while this row owns agreement among the enforcers that consume a valid declaration.

SR-034Kit scripts run on stdlib plus ledger-declared dependenciesre-accept owed

Requirement

Every kit script shall run on a clean Python 3.11+ using the standard library plus only those non-stdlib dependencies declared as a reviewed row in the dependency ledger.

Rationale

Realizes SN-011 — the kit must impose no *unargued* dependency stack on a downstream repo to run its checks, but a blanket ban is itself a design constraint that can force a worse hand-rolled alternative than a well-chosen tool, so the bar is a reviewed argument per dependency, not abstinence. Leaving the row at "stdlib-only" was rejected: it had already drifted from the standing ruling, leaving the registry and the ledger giving two answers to one question.

SR-040Per-phase routing and review dialre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator shall route each in-process session phase (PLAN/BUILD/REVIEW-A/REVIEW-B/DESIGN-CHECK/CRITIQUE) through its declared per-phase command template, falling back to the single declared command — surfacing the declared reviewer dial at run start without enforcing it.

Rationale

Realizes SN-026 (several model families selected per job, so that work benefiting from an independent second opinion is routed to a different family wherever that is configured) — two samples of one model share blind spots, so a review by the family that built the change agrees with it for the wrong reasons; cross-family routing is what makes the second opinion independent, and one model for every phase was rejected on that basis. Dispatch stays keyed off the in-process session phase because the alternative, a per-phase code branch, makes adding a phase a code change and so discourages adding one. THIS ROW CARRIED A RESUME-SURFACE SIZE TRIPWIRE AND NO LONGER DOES, and the two lenses that reached it are answered here rather than deleted with it. Both were premised on a session INHERITING a resume surface that grows across runs: a view must stay usable as its content volume grows (hat.UX-ENGINEER), and at 3am the reader of that surface is another automated step, which needs the growth legible from the artifact rather than from a human noticing (hat.UNATTENDED-OPS). Neither premise survives the one-engine coordinator — no session inherits a resume surface any more, and the status page is a generated integrator artifact whose size the generator owns, so there is no growing view to keep usable and no 3am artifact whose growth an automated reader must judge. The lenses are not overruled; their subject is gone. If a per-session resume surface is ever reintroduced, both apply again o… [187 more chars — read the registry row]

SR-049Derived stage from artifact statesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall derive the stage the project is currently at from the spine artifact states alone, caching it as a derived value — never accepting a hand-set one — with a post-attestation amendment dropping the derived stage exactly as a newly introduced draft does, and the pending-amendment count carried beside the draft count so the pending state never hides.

Rationale

SSOT applied to the gate itself: a hand-set marker can be bumped without the work; deriving it makes gate advancement mechanical (SN-004) and un-gameable (SN-008). The hybrid cache keeps the value readable on checkout; --check guards rot. SN-029 is a parent because this row's shall is the only place in the SR layer stating that an amended requirement drops the derived stage exactly as a newly introduced one does — SR-139 states which tiers are held, SR-140 what an acceptance record contains, and SR-148 loop selection, none of them the drop clause.

The page renders, in this order: the pending open items that queued or claimed work items cite in their needs, as decision briefs beside the queued or claimed rows citing them, preceded by an integrity notice naming and linking the pending items that no queued or claimed row cites, the page claiming an empty queue only when there is neither; every SR whose chain holds a row owing a first approval or drifted from the approved snapshot, with the chain's per-cell before/after, a section with no changed cell stating that no cell differs from the approved snapshot and never reading as nothing changed; the audit list of every act-ledger entry naming a verdict, newest first, or None recorded; the pending owner actions; and, last, the Decisions to review section. SR-052Dashboard accessibility (rubric-adjudicated)re-accept owed

Requirement

The state view the delivered generators produce shall be operable and readable without a pointer or full color perception: every interactive element (tabs, expandable blocks, SVG nodes with detail panels) is keyboard-reachable and carries an accessible name (title/aria/visible text); no information is encoded by color alone (status/phase/type encodings carry a text or shape cue); text keeps readable contrast against its fill.

Rationale

Realizes SN-024 and SN-023 — an accessibility bar left unstated silently reads as no bar at all, so the obligation is stated here even though its clauses were not measurable when the row was written. They since became so, one clause at a time, which is why this row's method is mechanical: the thresholds are the child rows' and the acceptance is their chain. Keyboard operability, an accessible name per element, colour never the only channel, and a readable contrast floor are the charter's own subject, and no other lens in the roster names a measurable perceptual threshold — the UX pair reaches robustness (it does not overflow), never legibility. That dependency is CLOSED: the ACCESSIBILITY charter is ruled `always`, so the lens this row derives from is put to every decomposition — and it had already reached this row once SN-023 carried the `a11y` tag, which is why the gap is narrower than the unmeasurable-clauses opening suggests.

SR-139Approval as an ordinal over a derived spine stagere-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall express operator approval authority as a cumulative level naming the highest spine tier an operator still approves, compared against a separately derived SPINE STAGE via a declared, auditable rung ordering — every unreadable or out-of-range input resolving toward MORE operator involvement.

Rationale

The retired three-value enum could not express "TCs are operator-held but LLRs are not", and four tables each re-interpreted the same word with its own fail-safe direction. The failure that matters is a machine approving something an operator meant to hold, so every degrade has to point the same way — including the ones that look like kindness: clamping an out-of-range level toward 0 reads as "nothing is operator-held" and disarms every hold in the repo. The crossing attribution: B-02 is unarguable - the approval level IS the authority input, and every fail-safe clause here describes how that input is read when it is broken. B-05 earns its place on a test, not on the fact that everything here is delivered content: the acceptance clause "Level N holds exactly the tiers the SHIPPED TEMPLATE documents" is a claim about the package's own contents agreeing with its behaviour, which is falsifiable against the package alone with no authority act performed - the same package-wide property class SR-031 occupies. The objection this had to survive is the measured one: B-05 already carries about four fifths of the layer's references, so adding a row to it needs an observable that is genuinely AT the package, not a default. This row has one. That the imbalance itself may be wrong is a separate question about the frame rather than about this row, and it is recorded where such questions belong.

SR-140Each acceptance is recorded by a copy riding its own approval commitre-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall record each acceptance as a byte-identical copy of the accepted registries riding the same reviewed commit as the approval itself - so the commit, its date and its author come from git rather than from a cell, and the transition accepted and the acting reviewer that accepted it are distinguishable BY QUERY, an approval delegated to automation on a tier the declared approval level released from an operator one.

Rationale

Attestation STATE is already the row's own Status - spine_rules derives the spine STAGE from those cells and reads no other source - so a separate ledger is a second home for a fact the row already carries, and three of its seven columns duplicated cells outright (Decision=approved|meaning IS Status; superseded IS SupersededBy). What a ledger gets right is the BASELINE ITSELF: answering 'has this been approved' by walking git for the newest commit where a row read Verified is sound only while every amendment flips its row in the same commit - which is neither the sanctioned staged-amendment path nor the approval ladder, so the walk returns HEAD and the diff is empty BY CONSTRUCTION on exactly the rows a sitting exists to judge. The record is therefore a whole-file copy of the accepted registries into docs/archive/last_approved/, riding the SAME reviewed commit as the approval. Three things follow. First, the commit, its date and its author come FROM that commit, so no cell has to carry them and no cell can lie about them. Second, the record is diffable by every git tool and by eye - a record only a script can read is a record only a script can audit. Third, the copy MUST ride the approval commit, because riding it is the only thing that makes "this copy is what was blessed" decidable. Anti-laundering rests on the MIRROR INVARIANT - any commit touching the record must leave it byte-identical to its live counterpart, so the only way to write text INTO the record is to write it … [1713 more chars — read the registry row]

Whole files rather than extracted rows is what makes "snapshot file == live file at the copy commit" DECIDABLE - LLR-178 carries that mirror invariant - and it is also what makes the UNANCHORED rule decidable, because the copy keeps each row's own Status cell, so a live row claiming approval whose snapshot copy reads below it is an approval that never rode a copy. unanchored_findings asks that of every tier SNAPSHOT_TIERS lists, the needs file's needs and stakeholders included, and reads the needs registry's copy under its legacy markdown carrier as present. Three refusals are load-bearing and each is the opposite of a convenient degrade: copy_live REFUSES to CREATE the directory without seed=True, because the first snapshot blesses whatever text is in the tree and must ride the owner'soperator's reviewed signing commit (reachable only from `intake.py snapshot --seed`); load_all returns None for an absent directory and RAISES on a file that exists and will not parse, because {} and None are opposite claims and the empty one reads as "re-bless everything with no diff shown"; and rows_for is the ONE place the None sentinel is collapsed, so no caller invents its own `or {}`. is_drifted/drifted_cells delegate the cell comparison to LLR-158's split_changed_cells and arm on the APPROVED half only. stamp() is advisory and derived FROM GIT rather than from a file, so it can never quietly become the ledger this mechanism replaced; every arm degrades to ("", ""). SR-140's two remaining record fields come from the same two places and neither is a cell: the TRANSITION is the copy's Status read against live's (the comparison above), and the ACTING REVIEWER is the AUTHOR of the commit that wrote the copy - which is why the copy must ride the approval commit and why the author is queried from git rather than stamped, since a stamped reviewer is a claim and a commit author is a record. unanchored_findings joins the integrity failure set, so it fails the always-on --strict-integrity floor at every stage; it is vacuous until the record holds a registry, so a tree that has signed nothing is never redded by it.

SR-144Every lane close is a terminal state with an immutable recordre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall close a lane that cannot finish into a TERMINAL partial state that merges like any other branch, with one immutable per-close report naming the claimed outcome, the reason, the commit range and the keep/discard split — refusing a report that declares neither a split nor an explicit deferral, refusing a second close of the same event rather than overwriting the first, and refusing a close whose claim is other than one work item.

Rationale

Five successive dedup mechanisms leaked because each reconstructed the return event from a MUTABLE proxy; a document that never moves dissolves the class instead of mitigating it. The refusals are what make "immutable" a property rather than a claim. The split is a field because its absence once merged rejected code onto trunk: silence about it is different from saying "I could not judge", and only silence is unactionable. A claim a dead lane never releases is C-UNA-3's deadlocked-until-morning case, and the immutable per-close record is C-UNA-5's answer to a failure that pages nobody — a close no one can read is externally indistinguishable from a run that finished.

Rationale 1% of the words changed
Two rules decide the shape. A judge's brief must not carry the claim under judgement as its premise - a leaked self-assessment anchors the judgement to it - so every value is registry-, git- or report-derived and the one claim shown - the lane's report - is the template's own labelled subject. And a HALF-filled brief is worse than the generic prompt: hollow sections read as an investigation that was run and found nothing, which is the expensive way to be wrong, so there is no placeholder path at all. The discriminator is a declared cell rather than a SpecRef shape because that inference is unsound - an amendment to a test-case row and a red-TC census row both cite the TC registry while their briefs give contradictory instructions - and rather than a Title substring because that is the `NEEDS-HUMAN``NEEDS-OPERATOR` fold (LLR-161).

Rationale 0% of the words changed
A vocabulary that several layers read must sit below all of them. This one used to be defined in the module that claims lanes, merges branches and moves specs, which meant every reader of the table imported a mutation coordinator to reach it - including the dashboard, a render leaf that writes nothing and must not be able to. That import was an edge of the strongly connected component the runtime scripts form, and it ran in the one direction a layered system forbids outright: a view into a lifecycle service. Moving the definition down cuts the edge at its cause rather than documenting it, and it removes two modules from the cycle in one act, because the render leaf was the whole route by which the dashboard facade reached the coordinator. The component tag is single deliberately: the shared kernel's ownership question is open, but the station flow is not ambiguous - the modules that ship it are all in this component - so this row states an owneroperator instead of inheriting a four-way usage tag that would suppress the cross-component seam rule on its own edges. The shared kernel's ownership question has since been settled elsewhere, and the reconciliation it owes this row is a recorded confirmation, not a tag move: the tag STAYS `CMP-008`, unmoved and NOT added to the declared shared-kernel surface. Unlike config/git/registry/ladder/stage, this module has exactly one real cross-component consumer - scripts/traj_panels reading the render leaf's own vocabulary - and that single edge was already given its own declared, policed seam (IF-093) authored alongside this row for precisely that reason. Folding it into the kernel declaration instead would silence an edge this row went out of its way to keep visible, for no benefit.

SR-146Prompts are reviewable files with a per-session audit trailre-accept owed

Requirement

Every prompt the delivered loop launches or an attended launcher renders as a review or critique brief shall be a shipped, reviewable file with strictly filled slots — listed by digest in a freshness-gated generated catalogue, each loop session recording which template it used and the fingerprint of what it rendered to.

Rationale

Prose steers the sessions this loop launches and had been reviewable only by reading Python source, which makes the process trusted rather than inspectable. The audit trail is the part that makes the move useful rather than cosmetic: without a per-session digest, "which instruction did this session see" stays an inference. (The argv-vs-shell-string transport decision is design, and lives one tier down in LLR-163.) C-SEC-5 requires that content composed for dispatch to an external model runner carry a DECLARED inclusion rule rather than an implicit one — a prompt assembled inside source is an unreviewed egress path no write-side gate covers, and shipping it as a reviewable file with a digest is what makes that rule readable.

Each `## ` section's next line declares its served tiers as `<!-- tiers: ... -->`, with `*` serving every tier. It composes, in home order and without that declaration line, every-tier sections and sections serving the rows judged: `_judged_tiers` derives first-approvalfirst-acceptance tiers from its `--approves` registry walk, and amendment tiers from the rows shown. `combined_values` composes each section through `compose`, so its first-approvalfirst-acceptance and amendment sections carry their own questions. An absent or unreadable home, a section without a tiers declaration, a home with no section, or a home serving none of the judged tiers refuses the brief naming that home; there is no fallback. Judging briefs order no act: a first-approvalfirst-acceptance brief derives neither an approval-registry token nor its per-token row map, and amendment aftermath identifies each verdict mark for a later turn. A CLARITY verdict is later re-anchored, naming its verdict on a held rung; a released-rung MEANING verdict it blesses is marked `MEANING+BLESS`; a held MEANING verdict is recommended to the owner.operator.
Rationale 1% of the words changed
Two rules decide the shape. A judge's brief must not carry the claim under judgement as its premise - a leaked self-assessment anchors the judgement to it - so every value is registry-, git- or report-derived and the one claim shown - the lane's report - is the template's own labelled subject. And a HALF-filled brief is worse than the generic prompt: hollow sections read as an investigation that was run and found nothing, which is the expensive way to be wrong, so there is no placeholder path at all. The discriminator is a declared cell rather than a SpecRef shape because that inference is unsound - an amendment to a test-case row and a red-TC census row both cite the TC registry while their briefs give contradictory instructions - and rather than a Title substring because that is the `NEEDS-HUMAN``NEEDS-OPERATOR` fold (LLR-161).

Detail 0% of the words changed
Round accepts only a full-lane review with no prior findings or a narrow review that names the prior findings file. render_review strictly fills the shipped reviewer template with the work-item specification, lane range, scratch location, optional review rubric and verdict destination; an empty derived set is a valid round, renders no test command, and states that the row touches no code; listed evidence and reported gaps render beside the test command; render_critique strictly fills the shipped critique template with the work-item specification and named rubric. Both refuse a missing specification, unreadable or empty named input, or unfilled template slot before a brief is written. review_refusal accepts only a verdict bound to the reviewed full commit after the shared review-line reader accepts exactly one line whose keyword, in any case, is VERDICT, in exactly the canonical form `VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`, whose count matches the finding lines the review scorer reads from declared-severity brackets and whose changes request names a finding. round_path chooses the next ordinal lane round filename, file_review writes only ana acceptedrecorded verdict as that round record when the round reader reads its lane path back as that lane's scope, and lane_commits resolves commits on a branch and requires the base to be an ancestor of the reviewed commit. A first plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when alone, opens with that commit, and refuses a missing rubric, plan or specification, a missing or beyond delta, a coverage failure, or a third round. A second plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when and the first critique's finding identifiers, never their text, uses convergence stance, and refuses a revision that leaves a first-critique finding neither covered nor excluded. A single-plan brief strictly fills the shipped single-plan template with the specification, ordered Done-when clauses, required registry references, and one planner output path; a revision additionally labels the committed plan and latest filed critique findings as claims under judgement. It refuses a missing specification, Done-when, plan or critique, or an unfilled slot. A critique record is filed only when it is bound to an ancestor that holds the plan and has the verdict form; a pass record is written only from committed cited records, passing plan coverage, and a passing delta, after an approval or an accepted dismissal of every blocking and major second-round finding. At the cap, a dispute findings file is written only from the committed second critique, giving each blocking and major finding the identifier of its position among all critique findings, its text verbatim, and a declared position; it refuses another identifier set or an existing file. The second plan critique's brief never carries the first critique's verdict or any finding's text. A review round is ordinary by default or convergence: ordinary emits no stance line, while convergence emits one fixed stance line after the range and refuses a narrow scope or unknown stance before writing a brief. An ordinary review reading scope reads the delegated-decisions record and filed plan critiques, while a convergence scope excludes both; a convergence render refuses a reviewer template whose reading-scope command does not carry the review-record exclusion exactly once. The scope critique names the component and interface registries, derived architecture, runtime flows, and dependency ledger, marking an absent registry; the single-plan brief and scope critique render their registry lines from one declared set. A plan critique ties every severity class to a normal-use-reachable defect: a fail-open, data-loss, or security path counts only when a supported workflow or the kit's own routes reach it, and a rare or contrived path is MINOR at most or dismissed. Its confirming round treats a new finding as BLOCKER or MAJOR only when it is a reachable fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when gap; anything else is MINOR. A finding line bearing the convergence-class tag defined by LLR-311 is filed and counted as one finding under the unchanged verdict grammar.

Method 1% of the words changed
Drive the real loop against a fake agent CLI over throwaway git repos for the disposition, red-TC and amendment briefs, and capture what the session was actually handed: the brief its row declares rather than the worker assignment. Assert the session writes the typed verdict line the brief demands to the path the brief named and commits it under the row's result trailer, ending the run done; that a session committing the trailer with no verdict, or with a label outside the brief's closed enum, does not complete; that a row whose declared brief cannot be filled is held for aan human,operator, with no session run, the reason printed and nothing committed under the row; and that a row declaring no brief builds from the worker assignment. Compose each routed brief in process and assert each slot carries its real derivation: for the disposition brief, the lane's report verbatim, the closed spec and the commit facts; for the red-TC brief, the live census joined to each TC row's Method, Expected and Evidence and to the obligation its targets name; for the consolidation brief, the whole cluster, the other open rows, the cited SR and LLR text (a stated literal when the cluster cites none), the overlap findings, the recorded and current digest pairs and what earlier consolidations absorbed; for the first-approvalfirst-acceptance brief, the whole chain of each SR holding a scoped row, the scoped `Drafted` rows marked as the question, a held or out-of-scope row labelled as not this session's and contributing no registry, an unrelated chain left out, no snapshot command, no 'BY YOU', no Status flip, and the later act turn named; TC-368 verifies act-side command quoting and registry scope, and TC-321 verifies act-side completion. Assert no `{slot}` survives in the composed disposition, red-TC, amendment and first-approvalfirst-acceptance text. Then drive the refusals, each returning its reason and never a partial brief: a clean close with no per-close report, a report with no typed `commit_range`, a census that has come clean, a TC row missing a listed cell, a target with no normative text; a first-approval,first-acceptance, amendment or consolidation row declaring no `Adjudicates` scope, a first approval whose scoped rows are all settled, gone from the spine or held for the owner,operator, and an amendment none of whose scoped rows still differs from its approved copy; a consolidation with no `Digests` cell, a cluster row no longer queued, and a cluster whose overlap has dissolved. Pin the discriminator: two rows with an identical SpecRef and different declared `Brief` cells compose differently. Pin the routing both ways: the routed set equals the shipped set and each routed brief names a shipped template, every brief a mint declares is shipped and every routed brief is declared by a mint, a row declaring `conflict`, which the kit no longer ships, refuses as an unknown brief, and an absent or unknown brief refuses. Pin each brief's typed verdict grammar: a well-formed line is accepted, and an absent file, a missing machine line, an out-of-enum label or a missing counter is refused with its reason. Pin the amendment arm's scope: the amendment mint writes the rows it routes as the row's `Adjudicates` scope, and a one-row mint's brief renders that row alone while another row's unadjudicated drift stays out of it, and a row hanging under two SRs is rendered once. The amendment arm covers two seams: IF-124, the `last_approved` baseline read - the brief carries the snapshot as its anchor, naming for each registry shown the commit that last wrote that registry's copy rather than the newest write anywhere in the snapshot, only approved cells reach the judge, and with no snapshot the brief holds and says FIRST APPROVAL rather than fabricating an anchor; and IF-075, the re-attestationre-acceptance model its before/after listing is read from. The amendment arm also renders a need, assumption or surrogate row in its scope with its drifted approved cells before and after, and leaves out a drifted row of those tiers that the scope does not name. A scoped row removed from the live registry while its recorded copy holds it approved is briefed as a removal, in a chained tier and in an unchained tier, for the single-kind amendment and combined classes; a present undrifted scoped row still drops beside it, and a scope token naming a row in neither home refuses, naming it. test_no_judging_brief_orders_an_act composes the first-approval,first-acceptance, released and held amendment, and combined briefs and finds no snapshot command, no 'BY YOU' and no Status flip, while naming the later act turn. Compose a first-approvalfirst-acceptance brief over an LLR and amendment briefs over an SR and an SN. Assert each carries the every-row questions and its own tier section, but no other tier section, and that a combined first-approvalfirst-acceptance section carries its rows' questions. Point the renderer at a substitute home and assert that its text is carried, a change changes the brief, and an absent home, directory, undecodable file, section with no tiers line, or home serving none of the judged tiers refuses naming that home. Assert no question opening appears in any prompt template or spine-authoring skill copy.

SR-147One machine-parseable carrier for the requirement spinere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall hold every spine tier in one machine-parseable representation, reached by a migration proven cell-for-cell over the live registries before the new representation becomes authoritative.

Rationale

THE ROW STATES ONE OBLIGATION, and the migration history - the two prior carriers and the cutover - is no part of it: normative history and a merged decision have no place at the requirement tier, and a rationale is where that account may live. The two-carrier split has no recorded rationale and costs on both sides. Reading 32 need rows takes ~166 code lines across 14 functions in 8 modules - six bespoke scanners, two of them F5 twins pinned by nothing but a docstring, which have already drifted once and rendered a phantom root in the dashboard - while reading all 436 SR+LLR+TC rows takes csv.DictReader. CSV also cannot represent the cells that actually exist: five hold a literal pipe, 552 hold commas, the longest is 1,553 characters, and an embedded newline has no representation at all. A structured carrier turns three integrity rules into properties of the parse - a duplicate id becomes a decode error, a ref list becomes a typed array (retiring the split-on-whitespace rule that read `and` as an orphan), and an empty cell becomes an absent key, so `unset` and `set to empty` stop being the same value. The converter is the migration's evidence, not its convenience: SR-129's 140-cell lesson is that an unproven representation change is exactly where a registry silently loses cells. ONE ROW because the single-carrier claim and its converter-proof are one contract — the converter is the migration's evidence — and the converter's mechanics already decompose to this row's LLR chain;… [330 more chars — read the registry row]

SR-148Autonomous loop work selection: what it derives from, and in what orderre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall select exactly one work item for each assignment an unattended run admits from the repository's tracked registries and git history alone, in this order: ready adjudication rows first, as a stable partition applied at admission rather than by renumbering the ruled rank table; then unresolved handback records; then the earliest incomplete spine tier in SN-to-SR-to-LLR-to-TC order; then implementation work after test-case layout is complete — with the eligible set and its order deterministic, an item whose declared safety, policy or plan-mode inputs are missing, undeclared or contradictory failing closed for that item alone, operator holds applied only from the declared approval level, nothing admitted past an operator-held stop, no prose surface and no predefined track in the derivation, no hand-curated next-work or run-phase pointer surface shipped for any live instruction or executable surface to read, write, validate, generate or link, and the status surface a session reads generated and freshness-gated rather than hand-copied.

Rationale

Without one precedence rule, the same repository can resume into implementation while returned obligations or prerequisite requirement tiers remain unresolved. That produces work against stale intent and makes repeated resumes select different next actions. A recorded selection class, source record and hold decision provide replayable evidence of the choice. ONE SR PER (need, property): the loop's work-selection invariant — what the next work derives from, in what order, and that no hand-curated pointer surface participates in it — is stated here and nowhere else, so no second row can drift from it. An explicit three-way partition was rejected: the partition already existed textually and still produced duplicated acceptance. The no-pointer obligation is stated for a migrated repository as well as a fresh scaffold, and the migrated half is the one that matters most: a fresh scaffold never had the files to keep, while an upgraded repository can retain the retired authority files and still pass. Fan-out re-stamp: this row states one decision — what an unattended run's next work derives from and in what order — and its children are the successive stages of that one selection, not separable contracts; the width is the deliberate consolidation of three rows that stated the same invariant into one, so re-splitting to satisfy the bound would restore the duplication the consolidation removed.

The route reads `Brief` and `Adjudicates` through the same normalization the merge uses, so a spelling or scope accepted by one cannot change the other’s bound. The row's DECLARED `Brief` cell selects the template (`intake` writes it at every adjudication mint that has a brief to declare; the report-less cancellation and clean-close spot-check arms declare none); `compose` fills it through `prompts.fill`'s strict both-ways check and `agent_loop.session_body` is the single fork BOTH routing arms take, so a claimed adjudication row gets the same brief whether or not a routing registry is configured. Each assembler returns `(values, None)` or `(None, reason)` and NEVER a partial: `disposition_values` walks SpecRef -> the closed spec -> its immutable per-close report -> that report's TYPED `commit_range` -> `git log`/`--name-status` clipped at the declared 80 lines, and refuses the clean-close spot-check arm because it writes no report; `red_tc_values` RE-RUNS `census.red_tc_census` rather than remembering it, joins each line through `census.parse_red_tc` to the TC row's Method/Expected/Evidence and to the SR/LLR text its targets name, and refuses a census that has come clean. A refusal is a HOLD, never a fallback: `session_body` returns the reason and `agent_loop.route_session` prints it on the stop banner and returns `EXIT_NEEDS_HUMAN``EXIT_NEEDS_OPERATOR` with no session run, so a judge is never briefed as a builder; only a row declaring no brief builds from the worker assignment. EVERY shipped brief is routed through an assembler, including done-when and combined: `conflict` was RETIRED rather than filled (it had a template and a verdict grammar and never a mint, an assembler or a reader for the `needs=` its own grammar demanded), and `consolidate_values` composes the consolidation brief from the row's `Adjudicates` cluster re-derived LIVE - every row of that cluster or none, and a cluster whose overlap has dissolved refuses rather than briefing a session about a contradiction that no longer exists. `amendment_values` renders the approved-cell before/after of the drifted rows `trace.reattest_model``trace.reaccept_model` finds, BOUNDED by the row's `Adjudicates` scope, which the amendment mint writes from the rows it routes exactly as the first-approvalfirst-acceptance mint does: a row declaring no scope refuses rather than reading the empty cell as the whole tree, a scope none of whose rows still differs from its approved copy refuses naming them, and a row hanging under several SRs is rendered once, naming each chain; a scoped row that the recorded copy holds approved and the live registry no longer carries is briefed as a removal for the sitting to rule, in one block naming it removed, with its approved cells as the before and the removal as the after, its tier counted for the questions, baseline and aftermath as a drifted row's tier, and its identity the digest of its recorded approved text; a scope token naming a row that neither the live registries nor the recorded copy holds refuses the composition, naming the token; and a scoped row present live with no approved-cell drift drops out as before; its baseline line names, for each registry shown, the commit that last wrote that registry's snapshot copy (`baseline_snapshot.stamp` given the registry), never the newest write anywhere in the snapshot directory. For need, assumption and surrogate scopes, _unchained_amended_rows renders their drifted approved cells through tier_owing, and the amendment aftermath takes its held-rung arm from adjudication_action. QUESTION HOME. `tier_questions` reads `prompts/spine-questions.md` at render time for the `{questions}` slot that `first_approval_values``first_acceptance_values` and `amendment_values` return. Each `## ` section's next line declares its served tiers as `<!-- tiers: ... -->`, with `*` serving every tier. It composes, in home order and without that declaration line, every-tier sections and sections serving the rows judged: `_judged_tiers` derives first-approvalfirst-acceptance tiers from its `--approves` registry walk, and amendment tiers from the rows shown. `combined_values` composes each section through `compose`, so its first-approvalfirst-acceptance and amendment sections carry their own questions. An absent or unreadable home, a section without a tiers declaration, a home with no section, or a home serving none of the judged tiers refuses the brief naming that home; there is no fallback. Judging briefs order no act: a first-approvalfirst-acceptance brief derives neither an approval-registry token nor its per-token row map, and amendment aftermath identifies each verdict mark for a later turn. A CLARITY verdict is later re-anchored, naming its verdict on a held rung; a released-rung MEANING verdict it blesses is marked `MEANING+BLESS`; a held MEANING verdict is recommended to the owner.operator.
Rationale 1% of the words changed
Two rules decide the shape. A judge's brief must not carry the claim under judgement as its premise - a leaked self-assessment anchors the judgement to it - so every value is registry-, git- or report-derived and the one claim shown - the lane's report - is the template's own labelled subject. And a HALF-filled brief is worse than the generic prompt: hollow sections read as an investigation that was run and found nothing, which is the expensive way to be wrong, so there is no placeholder path at all. The discriminator is a declared cell rather than a SpecRef shape because that inference is unsound - an amendment to a test-case row and a red-TC census row both cite the TC registry while their briefs give contradictory instructions - and rather than a Title substring because that is the `NEEDS-HUMAN``NEEDS-OPERATOR` fold (LLR-161).

SR-149Retired-vocabulary refusal in authored surfacesre-accept owed

Requirement

The harness shall report every occurrence of a retired process tag in a live authored surface — naming the file and line and the vocabulary that replaces it, at a severity that warns by default and fails under --strict — reporting none in a declared historical, generated or attestation-quoting surface, nor in a line or file marked as a declaration site.

Rationale

Realizes SN-010 (a reader can navigate the documentation and trust it: navigable and honest). This check is a CONDITION of the vocabulary conversion rather than a follow-up, on measured evidence: an earlier sweep removed a retired-tag construct from this repo's own open-items registry and it REGENERATED within days, caught only by an audit. A ~2,500-edit conversion held in place by attention is a conversion that comes undone. The carve-outs are as load-bearing as the rule: history is not rewritten and an attestation is never re-worded, because a swept sign-off makes a signed record claim something was signed that was not. C-MNT-3 gives every declared vocabulary value exactly one normative definition in one home; a retired tag surviving in a live authored surface is a second, contradictory definition of the same word, which is why the earlier sweep regenerated within days when only attention held it.

SR-150Stakeholder-need cells stay in stakeholder languagere-accept owed

Requirement

The harness shall report each stakeholder-need `need` cell that contains an internal path, an implementation-only identifier or a process citation, naming the row and the offending phrase — at a severity that warns by default and fails only under --strict, exempting a name declared on a reviewed exception list that ships empty (a name that is itself a user-facing interface belongs in a need), and reporting nothing for acceptance or engineering-requirement cells, which SN-033 exempts by its own text.

Rationale

Realizes SN-033 — its approved acceptance commissions exactly this check, and until this row it did not exist. The need tier was measured clean when this landed (0 of 27 cells), and the row sits deliberately AHEAD of the SR re-tier's churn: locking the clean state in costs one warn-first step now; trusting a large re-statement pass not to dirty it costs an audit later. Warn-first is the ruled posture, not a softness — a form heuristic over approved stakeholder prose must not gate without an operator ruling, and that ruling has not been made.

Detail 0% of the words changed
Reads the needs registry through spine_carrier.load_needs (either carrier answers; an unreadable registry REFUSES loudly rather than scanning as empty). A registry that is PRESENT but yields zero scannable need cells - an empty file, or real rows with no need field - is reported VACUOUS rather than clean, since nothing else in the harness hard-fails an emptied registry at DevStg-Reqs; an absent registry stays the pre-scaffold clean skip and a -000-only scaffold registry stays a blank form. The three token classes are data (CLASSES), labelled with SN-033's own vocabulary so a finding names the class the acceptance names. Two scope decisions are deliberate and documented in the docstring: SN-### is NOT a process citation (the SN registry is the stakeholder's own document, so a need pointing at a sibling need keeps the reader at the stakeholder tier - the live SN-025 case), and a single-slash, dot-free token is a path only when it RESOLVES in the scanned tree (docs/archive names a real directory and reports; English either/or pairs like subjective/perceptual resolve to nothing and stay exempt). URL spans - scheme:// and scheme-less www. forms alike - are suppressed whole, so a path-shaped tail inside an external address never reports under any class; the span stops at prose delimiters (comma/semicolon) and the www. form requires a multi-label host, so a genuine token abutting a URL and a local www.assets/logo.png both still report. A sentence-final token's trailing full stop is stripped before the phrase is judged or reported, so its reviewed exception matches. One finding per token: a later class re-matching inside an already-reported span is the same phrase to rewrite. The exception list (docs/need-form-allow) requires the ' — <reason>' separator per entry, the literal em-dash with spaces (ALLOW_SEP) - a line authored with a plain hyphen, or with no separator at all, declares nothing, so a malformed entry can only ever fail LOUD, never silence a finding. Wired as check.py's need-form step at every bar with NO --strict promotion, deliberately unlike check_vocab's severity ladder: promotion is an owneroperator ruling, and the wiring says so.

SR-154Independent review routed across familiesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall obtain, when unattended work reaches integration, each review or critique verdict the declared policy requires from a session that did not author the work — resolved per in-process phase and tier from the delivered agent registry's declared (family x model x tier) rows and only while the declared consent surface that turns managed selection on is present, drawn from a different model family wherever one is configured, degrading only to the documented same-family mode — with every selection logged before launch and a non-converging rework loop escalated through the declared approval level, and, where a claimed work item is marked for an in-lane single plan, refuse build output at its making or landing until a pass record binds its plan and Done-when.

Rationale

Realizes SN-026 (cross-family second opinions — every prior carrier of this contract demoted as routing machinery, so the sn_refs join forced the mint; SR-155 cites SN-026 too, for the planner pair, but only this row states the second opinion itself), SN-024 (an author cannot judge its own output) and SN-006. One row because routing, scheduling, scoring and escalation are one delivered contract — that the second opinion happens, independently, or its absence is documented — whose mechanics are the component details below it. The row also carries SN-026's DECLARATION and CONSENT half — `docs/agents.toml`'s pair-rows and the `docs/agents-enabled` surface whose presence turns managed selection on. That half had ZERO textual occurrence anywhere in the SR layer while `orphans=0` still held, because an orphan count proves a need has a citing row and never that the row carries the whole need. Managed selection is opt-in by consent rather than by configuration alone: a repository that declares families without dropping the surface has declared a capability, not turned one on, and the row now says so where a check can read it. fan-out re-stamp: the single plan's independent critique is one obligation carried by its briefs and filing and by its gate; the routing children remain separate.

SR SR-154changed
AcceptanceCriteria 0% of the words changed
A declared review policy of N schedules N independent reviewer sessions; the declared (family x model x tier) pair-rows of the delivered agent registry are the only candidate source, and the declared consent surface's presence is what turns managed selection on — absent, managed selection is off and no row is resolved; present, exactly one row resolves per in-process phase and tier; a configured cross-family draw is preferred and its unavailability degrades to the documented mode, never a silent skip; every selection is logged before launch, never a silent model swap; rework iterates within the declared budget and pages per the declared approval level on exhaustion. The verdict that may clear integration comes from a session minted for that review, or, where reviewer retention is on and the declared final-reviewer setting selects persistence, from a round the coordinator recorded as final for the lane's retained final reviewer, over the whole lane, from its recorded claim to its reviewed tip; iteration rounds between full rounds review only rework since the last reviewed state, answer that round's findings, and never clear integration, whether their session was started fresh or resumed. Where a claimed work item is marked for an in-lane single plan, no build output is accepted at its making or landing until a pass record binds its plan and Done-when; the plan either covers every Done-when item or excludes it with a reason, declares an architectural delta of none, or one carried within its scope. One revision receives a fresh independent critique. If that second critique does not read as an approval, only an accepted dispute dismissal of every blocking or major finding permits the record; otherwise the item goes to the owner.operator. A plan or Done-when changed after the record requires a fresh record. Ticking a Done-when item, or adding evidence to it, does not require a fresh record. Work items whose plan mark is absent, empty, none or dual are not held by this planning requirement; an unrecognized mark is held.

The coordinator's session log records each session's phase and its exact commit range (`# commits: before..after`), and records a REVIEW session's full or narrow scope (`# review-scope: base..sha`); session_range and parse_range read the range, review_logs yields the gating span with it, and range_paths lists the paths the range changed with renames split. scope_offenders names every changed path other than the REVIEW session's own verdict file, the round file named for the session's train, ordinal and logged phase under any reviewed sha and tag; record paths are not exempt. Right after a REVIEW session the loop asks scope_offenders of the range it just took and, on any offender, stops the run needing aan humanoperator with the paths named; a session log is append-only evidence, so every reader takes each log as the commit that ADDED it recorded it (log_history, review_logs), never at the branch tip, and the merge ladder's review-scope rung first refuses by name any commit in the lane that modified or deleted a session log, then asks the same function of every REVIEW session log the branch committed (review_scope_refusal) and refuses the merge by name, an unreadable log or range refusing too. After a REVIEW or CRITIQUE session, uncommitted changes not present before it, other than the coordinator's own session log, fail the draw through the existing failed-draw path - the route cooled and the same phase re-drawn - with those paths stashed under one entry named for the session, so the re-drawn session starts clean; when that stash fails the run stops needing aan humanoperator with the paths and the failure named, and nothing is re-drawn. read_verdict reads the verdict blob as committed at HEAD in both arms, so an uncommitted verdict is never routed on; session_body binds an adjudication's composed request beside its verdict before the loop calls it; after the call, run_iteration records the loop call's success from call_succeeded in plan, and adjudication_bookkeeping calls record_outcome against those bound kinds and uses its returned why as the completion obligation: a failed call is recorded failed, keeps that obligation and does not read its verdict. logged_rounds reads each round at the end of its session's recorded range, and only when that range changed the round file: a later commit rewriting the file changes nothing the gate counts, a file its session never committed is no round, and a key whose logs record different phases or ranges yields none. done_when.items reads a spec's Done-when section, through kitlib.registry.done_when_section, as items: a list item with its continuation lines, or a prose paragraph, across subsections. changes compares a claim-time text with a later one after stripping ticks, strikethrough and whitespace; a later item carries a claim-time one when it equals it or extends it with evidence in the form closed specs use - appended text opening with an evidence separator (a dash, an arrow, a bracket, a bar or a check mark) and carrying an evidence token (a capitalised completion word from the closed set LANDED, DONE, MET, VERIFIED, SHIPPED, PASSED, FIXED and COVERED, a path or test id, a backticked name, or a commit sha) - while any other appended text, after closing punctuation or not, is a change; and every claim-time item not carried is reported as changed and every later item carrying none as added. The claim warns by name on stderr for each claimed row with no Done-when item and still claims. When a review round is composed, the brief gains a block quoting each change between the spec under active/<train>/ at the lane's base and the lane's own copy. At merge, intake evaluates each claimed non-adjudication row. An unreadable claim refuses the merge-time mint, naming why; the merge itself stands and recovery is a trunk-side fix. For an absent claim, intake emits its stderr line that the Done-when check did not run and mints nothing. For a readable claim whose closed Done-when changed against trunk's pre-merge copy under active/<branch>, intake proceeds through the existing arms: when no verdict line or owneroperator ruling in the merged tree binds the closed text's digest, it mints one brief-bearing done-when adjudication row, titled per row and branch so a re-run dedupes, with Adjudicates naming the closed work item and Context quoting each change; when a covering SUCCESSOR verdict carries Dispositions drafts, it mints the Done-when part's own drafts instead - the whole single-kind verdict or its one ## done-when section - and refuses repeated Dispositions inside that valid section or one supplying no draft. A sitting with no or repeated done-when section, or a DONE-WHEN line under another heading, is invalid, covers nothing, and leaves the uncovered arm to mint the goalposts row. review_logs reads the resolved final-reviewer mode once per call through reviewer_dials and passes it to every REVIEW log's gating_span, so all readers apply one mode.

RationaleEvery merge is judged from records - the verdict files, the Done-when checklist - and each of them could be changed by the lane being judged: a reviewer committing work beside its verdict, a later session rewriting an earlier round, a builder rewording its own Done-when. Nothing on a commit reliably names its role, but the coordinator's session log does, so the checks key on it and are re-derived at merge from what was committed rather than trusted from the loop. Reading a round as its session committed it removes the rewrite without adding a refusal. The Done-when claim rule warns rather than refuses because the intake mint still files its derived rows without a Done-when, and a refusal would park every one of them.

Round accepts only a full-lane review with no prior findings or a narrow review that names the prior findings file. render_review strictly fills the shipped reviewer template with the work-item specification, lane range, scratch location, optional review rubric and verdict destination; an empty derived set is a valid round, renders no test command, and states that the row touches no code; listed evidence and reported gaps render beside the test command; render_critique strictly fills the shipped critique template with the work-item specification and named rubric. Both refuse a missing specification, unreadable or empty named input, or unfilled template slot before a brief is written. review_refusal accepts only a verdict bound to the reviewed full commit after the shared review-line reader accepts exactly one line whose keyword, in any case, is VERDICT, in exactly the canonical form `VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`, whose count matches the finding lines the review scorer reads from declared-severity brackets and whose changes request names a finding. round_path chooses the next ordinal lane round filename, file_review writes only ana acceptedrecorded verdict as that round record when the round reader reads its lane path back as that lane's scope, and lane_commits resolves commits on a branch and requires the base to be an ancestor of the reviewed commit. A first plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when alone, opens with that commit, and refuses a missing rubric, plan or specification, a missing or beyond delta, a coverage failure, or a third round. A second plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when and the first critique's finding identifiers, never their text, uses convergence stance, and refuses a revision that leaves a first-critique finding neither covered nor excluded. A single-plan brief strictly fills the shipped single-plan template with the specification, ordered Done-when clauses, required registry references, and one planner output path; a revision additionally labels the committed plan and latest filed critique findings as claims under judgement. It refuses a missing specification, Done-when, plan or critique, or an unfilled slot. A critique record is filed only when it is bound to an ancestor that holds the plan and has the verdict form; a pass record is written only from committed cited records, passing plan coverage, and a passing delta, after an approval or an accepted dismissal of every blocking and major second-round finding. At the cap, a dispute findings file is written only from the committed second critique, giving each blocking and major finding the identifier of its position among all critique findings, its text verbatim, and a declared position; it refuses another identifier set or an existing file. The second plan critique's brief never carries the first critique's verdict or any finding's text. A review round is ordinary by default or convergence: ordinary emits no stance line, while convergence emits one fixed stance line after the range and refuses a narrow scope or unknown stance before writing a brief. An ordinary review reading scope reads the delegated-decisions record and filed plan critiques, while a convergence scope excludes both; a convergence render refuses a reviewer template whose reading-scope command does not carry the review-record exclusion exactly once. The scope critique names the component and interface registries, derived architecture, runtime flows, and dependency ledger, marking an absent registry; the single-plan brief and scope critique render their registry lines from one declared set. A plan critique ties every severity class to a normal-use-reachable defect: a fail-open, data-loss, or security path counts only when a supported workflow or the kit's own routes reach it, and a rare or contrived path is MINOR at most or dismissed. Its confirming round treats a new finding as BLOCKER or MAJOR only when it is a reachable fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when gap; anything else is MINOR. A finding line bearing the convergence-class tag defined by LLR-311 is filed and counted as one finding under the unchanged verdict grammar.

On git repositories, in modules registered as slow: a later commit rewriting a CHANGES-REQUESTED round to APPROVE, asserted to leave the governing identity unmoved, leaves the gate refusing; a verdict its logged session never committed is no round; a later session that commits a verdict-only rewrite and then rewrites the earlier session log to name that clean range is refused by name at the merge ladder, naming the log and the commit that modified it, and the gate does not clear; the merge ladder refuses by name, naming the session log and each path, a review range that changed files beside its verdict, through the ladder itself, and passes a clean one. Driving the loop with a fake agent: a clean review is accepted; a reviewer committing a file beside its verdict stops the run needing aan humanoperator and names the file; a reviewer leaving an untracked file fails its draw, the same phase re-drawn on another reviewer completes the round and the file is stashed under a named entry, while a stash that fails - driven through the loop with the reviewer holding the index lock - stops the run needing aan humanoperator with the paths named after exactly one review launch, and, called directly, neither cools the route nor arms a redraw; a reviewer and a critic each writing a CHANGES-REQUESTED verdict without committing it cause no rework build, and the re-drawn session's committed verdict closes the round. A claim of a row with no Done-when warns by name and still claims, and one with a Done-when is silent. A lane rewording its Done-when is flagged in its reviewer's brief; at merge an uncovered change mints one done-when adjudication row quoting both texts, idempotently, while a covered change mints no goalposts adjudication and a lane that only ticked with evidence mints none.

SR-155Contested planning rounds for marked workre-accept owed

Requirement

Where work is declared as contested planning, the delivered loop content shall produce the selected decomposition through a bounded round of two independently authored rival plans — cross-critiqued, mechanically coverage-compared and arbitrated by fresh sessions — committing the selected outcome atomically as registry-valid queued rows and surfacing a non-converging round through the declared approval level, never falling back to a single uncontested plan silently.

Rationale

Realizes SN-024 (a decomposition judged by a competing plan and an independent arbiter rather than its author), with SN-026 (the planner pair prefers distinct families), SN-002 (the selected outcome lands as registry-valid rows, not prose) and SN-006. One row because the dual-plan round is one delivered capability with one observable outcome class (SELECT or PAGE); its state machine, briefs, adapters and isolation rules are the component tier's. Fan-out re-stamp: the round is one delivered capability with one observable outcome class, and its children are the successive phases of that single round — planner pair, briefs, coverage comparison, arbitration, isolation, disposition — none of which an adopter can obtain, refuse, or observe independently of the round, so the child count measures the round's step count rather than a merge of contracts.

SR-156Bounded lanes narrowing to one gated landingre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall run exactly one work item per lane on bounded, mutually isolated lanes and narrow every lane back to the integration branch through one serial, fail-closed seam that runs the declared bar on the composed tree — parking a red candidate and stopping the queue loudly, draining claiming to a clean merged stop under a declared pause, and reconstructing claim and queue state from version-control history alone at any crash boundary, never a half-integrated authoritative state.

Rationale

Realizes SN-027 WHOLE — ready work fans out across bounded parallel lanes and that fan-out narrows to one serialized gated seam before anything lands, in the need's own words — with SN-008 (the seam is fail-closed) and SN-025 (recovery from version-control history alone). ONE DECISION PER ROW: "serial integration is one delivered contract" is sound for the SEAM, but lane execution, claim authority and the trunk-side mint of work-item identity are not the seam, and a row stating the seam alone leaves SN-027's FIRST half — bounded lanes, isolated working trees, a worker ceiling — stated nowhere. This row therefore states the whole lane LIFECYCLE (claim, run isolated, close, land), which is what closes that hole; the trunk-only authority contract sheds to SR-170. The two fail independently: a perfectly serialized landing that lets a lane commit a regenerated artifact satisfies this row and not that one. Terminal close is SR-144's and is not restated here — one SR per (need, property), and both rows sit under SN-027 — so what this row carries of it is only that a terminal branch still lands through the one serial seam.

RationaleEvery merge is judged from records - the verdict files, the Done-when checklist - and each of them could be changed by the lane being judged: a reviewer committing work beside its verdict, a later session rewriting an earlier round, a builder rewording its own Done-when. Nothing on a commit reliably names its role, but the coordinator's session log does, so the checks key on it and are re-derived at merge from what was committed rather than trusted from the loop. Reading a round as its session committed it removes the rewrite without adding a refusal. The Done-when claim rule warns rather than refuses because the intake mint still files its derived rows without a Done-when, and a refusal would park every one of them.

SR-157Spine and work-registry rules red the harness verdictre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report every declared spine and work-registry rule violation — broken joins, integrity and schema faults, leftover placeholders, requirement-form findings and work-item coherence contradictions — naming the at-fault row and cell, gating the declared failure set at the declared gate while advisory classes never change the exit code.

Rationale

Realizes SN-002 (the chain is mechanically verified, not asserted — this row is the boundary-level home of the verdict SN-002's acceptance asks for), SN-012 (optional registries and opt-outs cost a non-user nothing) and SN-025 (the tracked work-item graph the loop derives its next work from is kept coherent). One row because the adopter-observable contract is one: registry rules produce named findings at a declared severity; which rules, at which severities, is the component detail the rows below it decompose. Deliberate pair (census F6): the PB-format invariant itself is SR-015's; this row's decomposition carries the checker. Fan-out re-stamp: the delivered contract is one — a named, row-and-cell-attributed finding at a declared severity, gating or advisory — while the rule inventory it ranges over is open by this row's own acceptance ("a rule added at one of those sites is in this row's scope by default"), so the child count tracks the number of declared rules rather than the number of decisions this row makes, and would climb back through any bound a split bought.

SR-157 itself — no cell of this row changed

AcceptanceCriteriaEach declared registry rule violation is reported with row-level attribution; the declared strict set exits nonzero at its gate and advisory classes never join the exit code; absent or placeholder-only optional registries and declared opt-outs are vacuous; the declared verification vocabulary (including Critique) is accepted and an unknown value fails. The declaration this is read against is the rule inventory the delivered checkers themselves publish — the id shapes, the required cells and the closed vocabularies (with the interface and component entries advisory by their own recorded ruling), the strict flag families and their stated exit contracts, the gating form and provenance findings beside the never-gating paraphrase and acceptance advisories, and the work-item coherence rules with their declared opt-out — each recorded at its declaration site, not restated here. A rule added at one of those sites is in this row's scope by default: an unreported one is a finding against this row, not an amendment to it.

Whether a row that passes every rule says something worth relying on is not this row's claim.

SR-159Declared-architecture connectivity gaps are reportedre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report declared-architecture connectivity gaps — an unresolvable interface row, an undeclared endpoint or direction, a cross-component import no declared interface covers, an invalid spec interface citation, and a top view past its declared bound — warn-first with --strict gating, vacuous where the optional inventories are absent.

Rationale

Realizes SN-023 (the parts' connections are as much of the truth as the requirement tree, checked mechanically warn-first — the need's own words), SN-002 (interface rows stay resolvable) and SN-012 (opt-out and vacuity keep the layer free for non-users). One row: the delivered contract is one connectivity verdict; the checkers below it are its decomposition.

SR SR-159changed
AcceptanceCriteria 0% of the words changed
Malformed or unresolvable IF rows are findings; undeclared endpoints, uncovered cross-component edges, invalid spec citations and an oversized top view warn plain and fail --strict; declared opt-outs and small or absent inventories are vacuous; declared seams render without changing the verdict. The rules and their opt-outs are read off their declaration sites, not restated here: the interface and component id shapes and the off-spine back-link to the spine sit on the always-on integrity floor and join --strict, their required-field entries and enums staying advisory by the recorded warn-first sequencing; the connectivity rules join every module of the generated architecture inventory against the declared interface endpoints (a module resolving to no endpoint is the "connectivity undeclared" warn), report a cross-component import no declared interface covers and a spec interface citation resolving to neither a declared seam nor the intra-module escape, and hold the top view to its declared bound (warn plain, error under --strict); two declared opt-outs and a per-module source/sink honesty valve carve the layer out. A connectivity rule added at one of those sites is in this row's scope by default. Carved out of that default (owner(operator ruling 2026-08-15, second-read M1): the interface endpoint-pair cells and the closed discrete/variable Signal vocabulary are SR-162's observables — their resolution against the declared external frame is SN-037's need, stated there in the need's own words — while the generic required-field and closed-vocabulary checker those cells ride stays SR-157's; a rule landing at those two cells belongs to those rows, not this one.

SR-161Each decomposition round is reviewed against its applicable perspectivesre-accept owed

Requirement

When a decomposition round is reviewed, the delivered planning content shall provide every applicable declared perspective's question in the decomposition brief and require the sitting's review record to name the outcome for each perspective.

Rationale

A decomposition produced from one perspective can look complete while omitting security, operations or first-use failures. The hats roster and the planning briefs already supply the applicable questions, and the sitting's review record preserves their outcomes; a separate machine-readable coverage record and checker would duplicate that review without improving its adequacy judgment. Hat-Refs remain the row-level provenance for perspectives that raised a requirement. This applies the operator ruling of 2026-09-06, re-affirmed 2026-10-13.

A sitting brief for a decomposition round carries every declared perspective question applicable to that round and asks the verdict to name one outcome for each perspective. The verdict's per-perspective outcome lines are neither row-ruling lines nor machine lines, so a verdict carrying them parses to the same rulings and judged rows as one without them. A decomposition round's sitting brief also carries a named stopping-boundary line, asking the verdict to state, for each retained chain, why further splitting would only paraphrase or duplicate; a round with no roster or no applicable perspective carries it beside its no-perspective line, because the stopping decision rests on no perspective. A stopping-boundary line is likewise neither a row-ruling line nor a machine line, and nothing checks for it: a retained chain with no stopping reason is a finding for the review of the verdict. A decomposition round judges a system requirement awaiting first approval or an approved stakeholder need whose text is amended; another judged set carries no perspective question and no stopping-boundary line. The applicable set combines each amended need with each need named by a system requirement the sitting judges, including an amended system requirement, widens each need by the authoring work item's declared tags, and evaluates each need alone. A first-approvalfirst-acceptance or amendment row a route mints records the declared tags of the work items that route names as its authors, and those tags stand in place of the row's own classification; a route naming no authoring work item records none, and the row widens by its own tags. Such a row minted from a minted row passes that record on, so the minted and in-lane sittings for one system requirement reach one perspective set wherever the authoring work item is named. Questions and the stopping-boundary line fill the perspective slot only when the sitting template declares it; a template without that slot composes unchanged. A sitting composed from several judgement kinds carries the questions and the stopping-boundary line once, after its last section, and says under which section the verdict writes those lines. Outside a decomposition round the roster is not read. An absent roster yields its no-perspective line, while an unreadable existing roster refuses a round's composition only when its template declares the perspective slot, and names the roster.

SR-165The component partition carries a reproducible derivation recordre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered planning content shall leave, with every component partition it produces, a machine-readable derivation record in the tracked component registry rather than session prose — the candidate partitions considered, the declared objective and constraints they were scored against, each candidate's score, the selected partition, and the operator ruling that named the components and adopted it — such that a live component row whose record omits any of those elements, or a selection the recorded scores do not rank first without a recorded operator override, is a reportable finding.

Rationale

Realizes SN-040 — a free-form partition leaves no record of the alternatives weighed, so the next reviser cannot tell load-bearing boundaries from accidents; the record is what lets the choice be re-examined. SN-040 had no citing SR, even as the P5 partition work performed exactly this record. Reproducibility is stated as a recomputation from the record's own declared inputs, not as a reviewer re-running a model session, because only the former can fail. B-05 alone: the operator ruling is an element the record must carry, not an observable the system states at the authority input, which is SR-139's and SR-140's ground.

Extends the existing component pass — the one home that already reads docs/requirements/components.toml and already emits CMP findings — with the derivation-record rules SR-165 states, rather than adding a second reader of the same registry. Per live CMP row: the record must declare the candidate partitions considered, the objective and the constraints they were scored against, a score per candidate, the selected partition, and the humanoperator ruling that named the components and adopted it; a missing element is one finding naming the row AND the element. Two derived rules on top of presence, because presence alone is satisfiable by a record that says nothing: (1) THE RANKING RECOMPUTES — re-rank the recorded candidates from the record's own objective, constraints and scores and compare with the recorded order, a mismatch being a finding, which is what makes the record falsifiable without a reviewer re-running a model session; (2) A SELECTION THE SCORES DO NOT RANK FIRST is a finding unless the record carries aan humanoperator override naming that choice, so a legitimate "the scores said A, the humanoperator chose B" is expressible and an unexplained one is not. Vacuous by construction on a project declaring no components, and on the example -000 rows. NOT BUILT YET: the record cells do not exist on the CMP schema today — recorded as open debt on this row and TC-166; SR-165 carries Test verification precisely because the check is mechanizable, and this is the debt that verification incurs, recorded rather than silently owed.
Rationale 1% of the words changed
The check belongs where component_findings already is for the reason the census keeps applying: a second module reading components.toml would be a second answer to "is this partition recorded", and the two would drift. The recompute is the load-bearing half — an element-presence check passes on a record whose scores contradict its own conclusion, which is the exact failure SN-040 exists to catch (the next reviser cannot tell load-bearing boundaries from accidents). The override arm is what stops the recompute rule from forbidding humanoperator judgement: the requirement is that a departure from the scores is RECORDED, never that it is disallowed.
