SR-166The delivered package materializes where its manifest declares it willre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered package shall be consumable at its own declared shipped-file manifest — every file the manifest names materialized at its declared destination in a fresh scaffold, and this repository's own instance carrying the structure of the template it ships — with a declared destination a fresh scaffold does not carry, and a structural divergence between the shipped template and this repository's instance, each failing rather than degrading the delivered package silently.

Rationale

Realizes SN-001 (an adopting team gets a working, gated, requirement-traced process without hand-building the tooling — which presupposes that what arrives is whole) and SN-007 (the kit is held to the standard it ships). The observable is B-05's own artifact-shaped one: the package exists, is complete, and is consumable at the manifest it declares. Verification evidence is named rather than owed: tests/test_bootstrap.py drives bootstrap.py's MAPPING against the file lists a fresh scaffold must carry, and tests/test_dogfood_sync.py pins this repository's own instance against the template it ships, so the manifest cannot declare one thing and the package deliver another. Deliberately distinct from its two neighbours: SR-163 asks why each shipped file EXISTS (SN-038, purpose coverage), SR-010 asks whether the generated scaffold runs GREEN, and this row asks whether what was promised ARRIVES WHERE IT WAS PROMISED. DELIBERATELY NARROW: manifest PRESENCE — a named source the package does not carry, and a shipped file the manifest does not name — is SR-163's alone, reported under its configurable warn-versus-gate policy, because two rows prescribing different outcomes for one observable is a contradiction an implementer can only resolve by violating one of them. What is left is what SR-163 does not ask: not whether a file is accounted for, but whether it LANDS — at its declared destination in a fresh scaffold, and in this repository's own instance of the template it ships.

Rationale 0% of the words changed
OwnerOperator ruling D-8 (OI-16, inversion confirmed 2026-08-13) replaced the F5 rule, under which a shared module was rejected so each script stayed independently copy-able. F5 bounded nothing: a 2026-08-12 census found the declared-line reader with five homes carrying a false claim of equivalence, is_example with three homes one of which crashed on None, and a 270-line spec-folder reader copied verbatim into three modules — a copy that had itself drifted by the time this row landed. Equality pins could contain that class but never shrink it. The INVERSION is the load-bearing half: D-8's literal step 2 (import from bootstrap.py) is unbuildable because bootstrap.py is deliberately absent from its own MAPPING, so a shipped script importing it would raise ModuleNotFoundError on a fresh scaffold while passing in the kit — the exact failure this repo shipped once when MAPPING omitted schedule.py. So the package ships like any other sibling and the scaffolder imports FROM it. SR-170Shared authority surfaces are the serial actor's alonere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall write the shared records it derives - the compiled activity log and the generated project-state artifacts - only from the serial merge step and only against the merged tree, never from a parallel work branch.

Rationale

ONE DECISION PER ROW: a shared serial actor is a shared MECHANISM, not one decision. This row holds the EXCLUSIVE-WRITER contract alone; ordering-and-all-or-nothing is SR-173's and identity allocation SR-174's, each with its own children. Realizes SN-027's serialization guarantee at the surfaces where a parallel writer would actually corrupt something, with SN-010 (the status surface a human reads regenerates at the seam, never on a lane), SN-008 (a first failure stops loudly rather than half-regenerating) and SN-025 (the surface a session reads is generated, never hand-copied). The serial LANDING (SR-156) and the rule that shared authority surfaces regenerate only there are two contracts that fail independently, since a perfectly serialized landing that still lets a lane commit a regenerated artifact satisfies the landing row and not this one. The three surfaces sit in ONE row rather than three because they share one decision, not three: the serial trunk actor is their sole writer. That decision is already ruled for the identity mint — a work branch never mints a work-item id — and this row is its requirement-tier home, which it did not have. `phase` inherits the parent's 4, matching every child.

SR-171Bounded retry on a declared transient model limitre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall retry a declared transient provider limit under a bounded backoff, surfacing the wait so a throttled run is distinguishable from a wedged one, rather than ending the run.

Rationale

This obligation was live but stated ONLY in SR-026's acceptance cell, where it minted a requirement the shall never made. Deleting it would have dropped real behaviour, so it is stated here instead. Realizes SN-006 (a walk-away run survives the conditions it will actually meet - a rate limit is the ordinary one) and SN-025. The bound is what separates this from a retry loop: unbounded retry against a limit that is not transient is indistinguishable from a hang, which is the failure SN-006 exists to prevent. Surfacing the wait is the other half - a silent backoff and a wedged run look identical from outside. ONE `shall`, with both clauses kept: surfacing is stated as a property of HOW the retry happens rather than as a second obligation, which is the honest reading - an unsurfaced bounded retry and a wedge are indistinguishable from outside, so a retry nobody can see does not discharge this row. Whether surfacing is instead a decision that fails independently of the retry - a split rather than one obligation - is an open question for the sitting, flagged and not decided here.

SR-174Identity is allocated once and never re-issuedre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall allocate each identity it mints at most once. Work items are minted on the integration branch alone. The registry identities that parallel lanes author are drawn from one shared reservation record. No two concurrent actors receive the same identity, and an identity freed by a deletion is never re-issued.

Rationale

Identity allocation is its own decision, not a consequence of serialization: serializing the writer makes a COLLISION unlikely and does nothing about RE-USE, which is the half that silently re-points every commit message and archived document citing the freed id. The non-reuse clause has a `shall` of its own here rather than living in SR-170's acceptance, which is a cell that cannot mint a requirement. Contributes to SN-025 (the ready frontier ordered deterministically, so two readers of the same registry dispatch the same work) by supplying a work-item identity that names one record for every reader, before and after a deletion. It contributes to SN-027 by assigning the registry identities independently authored by parallel lanes from one reservation record, so concurrent lanes cannot receive the same identity.

Four triggers, serial by construction: (a) the approved/routed-cell diff on the merged commit via check_trajectory.staged_spine_amendments, whose walk covers the SR, LLR, TC, SN, DA and SUR tiers -> one adjudication row listing each changed row/cell/before-after (routed traced cells: SR SN-Refs and Boundary-Refs, LLR SR-Refs and TC Verifies per the declared cell split); (b) a merged spec carrying ## Handback -> the disposition row (outcomes cancel / defer / re-queue with drafted follow-up / surface an open item; NEVER minted for an adjudication row - no recursion, and handback.hand_back refuses the act itself); (c) the dispatcher's gap census -> concrete gap-closure rows, deduped against every existing row; (d) ana acceptedrecorded verdict in the merged range whose latest amendment ruling on a row is MEANING, blessed or not, on a rung the dial holds, with the row at the range's end differing from its approved-snapshot copy and either equal to the text the verdict's binding records or gone from its registry, yields, per landing and per registry, one queued owneroperator row and one pending open item naming every such row of that registry, their verdicts and the act's command, the item cited in that row's needs, in the mint's one commit. The command re-attestsre-accepts every row it names and never names a verdict, the act being the owner's,operator's, and the item's option (a) directs the owneroperator to name beside them any other row of the registry unanchored when the owneroperator acts. Every other non-refusing state writes nothing, and a row left over, one whose text differs from what its verdict bound or whose verdict bound none included, stays on the amendment row as any other record does. Where a landing owes an open item, through this trigger or a drafted [open_item] table, and the open-items registry is not the TOML carrier, the mint refuses by naming the carrier, writes nothing, including any amendment row the same landing owes, and the merge stands; recovery is converting the carrier and then sweeping the range. SR-178Text that has moved away from its acceptance record is reportedre-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall report any recorded artifact whose text has moved away from the copy recording its acceptance - stakeholder needs included - regardless of any Status movement.

Rationale

THE DRIFT half, separable from SR-140 in the direction that matters: a record that exists and rides its approval commit, with nothing ever comparing live text against it, satisfies SR-140 completely and leaves every later amendment invisible. That is not a hypothetical - it is precisely the failure the git-history derivation had, and the reason a baseline on disk was owed at all. REGARDLESS OF STATUS MOVEMENT is the load-bearing clause, not a qualifier. The amendment machinery watches the Status flip, and the sanctioned staged-amendment path deliberately does not flip - so a rule keyed off the flip returns nothing on exactly the rows a sitting exists to judge. Reporting against the recorded copy is the only reading that survives that, because the copy is a baseline OUTSIDE the live file and a walk over the live file can never be one. THE STAKEHOLDER-NEED RIDER is in the normative text rather than left to the acceptance because the need tier is the one a sitting most wants to hold and the one the amendment-watching rules were last to reach: each rule walks the tiers it is given, so without the clause the need tier is left off the walk and no rule reaches it. Needs are compared row by row under the same approved and traced split as every other tier. WHAT COUNTS AS MOVEMENT is one definition with one home, shared with the amend-without-flip guard: the id column and the Status cell are excluded STRUCTURALLY (the id is the join key rather than content, and folding Status in would … [231 more chars — read the registry row]

Detail 1% of the words changed
An approval that records what it blessed by COPYING the registries needs no canonical text to hash, no separator that cannot occur in a cell and no second exclusion list, so no digest engine sits behind this row — the comparison basis is discharged by split_changed_cells(csv_path, id_col, head, row) -> {"approved": {cell: (before, after)}, "traced": {...}}: the id column and Status are excluded STRUCTURALLY - the id is the join key rather than content, and folding Status in would make every flip read as an amendment and every amendment invisible behind its own flip - and the remainder is split by spine_cell_class, the SAME classifier the amend-without-flip guard reads, so the two can never disagree about what normative means. It is PUBLIC for exactly one reason: baseline_snapshot.is_drifted reads it as the drift basis (LLR-173), so the snapshot comparison and the staged-amendment guard are one rule with one home rather than two rules that agree until they do not. _APPROVED_TEXT names the one Status value whose row TEXT is approved (Approved — the status fold collapsed Verified and Planned into it) and requires the SAME value on both sides, so prose rewritten under an Approved row is never invisible. It returns the before/after PAIRS a brief has to render anyway, which is why it replaced a hash rather than being wrapped by one. Needs are compared row by row through the same basis, their approved and traced cells split like every other tier's. ONE TWO-TREE WALK feeds every reader that asks what a spine delta did: _spine_row_sides pairs each row's before and after side once, and four consumers read it — staged_spine_amendments (the rows whose approved text moved), staged_approval_acts (the rows that crossed INTO an approval claim, or arrived already making one), staged_drafted_rows (the rows a lane authored below approval, which the first-approvalfirst-acceptance mint is raised over) and lane_approval_refusal, which words the merge slot's approval-act refusals. The walk is shared rather than copied so that the set one reader EXEMPTS is the set another REPORTS, MINUS the de-approvals: an Approved -> Drafted withdrawal moves Status, so the amendment reader exempts it, but it blesses nothing, so the approval-act reader does not report it and staged_drafted_rows raises the re-approval it now owes instead. Subject to that one subtraction, an approval act is invisible to the amendment reader by construction, and a row that no reader saw is unrepresentable. The per-row judgement is stated once, in _approval_act, so the flip arm and the born arm are read side by side rather than as two branches of the walk that could drift apart. UNREPRESENTABLE WITHIN A DECLARED BOUND, and the bound is named rather than left as an absence — the walk's universe is a PARAMETER over two declared sets, not one set every reader shares. SPINE_CSVS is the THREE registries whose rows carry an id column and an approved text — system-requirements, low-level-requirements, test-cases — and is the walk's default, so staged_drafted_rows, and the first-approvalfirst-acceptance mint over it, read exactly it. APPROVAL_ACT_CSVS is those three PLUS stakeholder-needs and the assumptions registry's two tiers (assumptions and surrogates), and staged_approval_acts passes it, so the merge slot requires each approval act, including one on a need, to have ana acceptedrecorded verdict that judges its own rows. The need tier is inside because it carries the same status vocabulary and every approval act requires the same independent verdict. An unreadable claimed frontmatter is refused by name at the merge slot and at partial close rather than read as an unscoped lane; a lane that records no scope is judged only by its acted rows and copies, with no `Adjudicates` wording. AMENDMENT_CSVS is an alias of APPROVAL_ACT_CSVS rather than a second list, and staged_spine_amendments passes it, so the amend-without-flip warn and the intake amendment mint, which both consume that walk, cover the need, assumption and surrogate tiers beside the three; the warn's Hat-Refs arm stays structurally silent on those three tiers, none of which carries Hat-Refs. The mint additionally drops records the merged range already settled under LLR-364, while the pre-commit warn reads the unfiltered walk because it runs before any act. The three registries a snapshot anchors that no approval reader walks — interfaces, external, components — are listed in OUTSIDE_THE_APPROVAL_ACT: off-spine, their approval cells governed by their own rung rather than this one. The two lists are pinned as one exhaustive, disjoint statement, SNAPSHOTTED == APPROVAL_ACT_CSVS + OUTSIDE_THE_APPROVAL_ACT, against baseline_snapshot.SNAPSHOTTED's eight. A tier added to the snapshot therefore lands on one side or the other by a deliberate edit, and cannot reach no approval reader at all.

When an amendment-record walk returns records, the settled filter excludes only a record whose id is re-attestedre-accepted by an act-ledger entry added within the requested range, whose whole approved and routed traced cell sets at the range's after revision equal that row's approved-snapshot copy at that revision, and for which either no entry the range added after the latest re-attestingre-accepting one records a copy of that row's registry or omits its copy record (a legacy entry, whose copy set is unknown), or the row's routed traced cells at the after revision equal those at the before revision. An owneroperator row carries a held-MEANING record out of the amendment row. A later act copying the registry without re-attestingre-accepting the row cannot have absorbed an unattested change to its approved cells, only to its routed traced cells, so the first arm proves the copy is the re-attestingre-accepting act's own and the second proves the row's routed traced cells are the same at the range's two ends, whether the range is one squashed commit or many. The second arm's one limit: a routed traced cell moved before the re-attestingre-accepting act and restored after it is re-anchored by a later act's copy of the registry, as any traced refresh is, and the row settles. A row re-attestedre-accepted in the range whose routed traced cells moved in the range is not proven settled when a later act copies its registry, so it is minted even when its own act judged it. The comparison includes cells outside the net range diff. A tree that does not list the ledger supplies no acts, and a missing copy or a copy without the row leaves the record to mint. A listed ledger or snapshot copy that cannot be read or does not parse refuses the mint by naming the carrier and revision; it is never treated as absent. The same filtering result serves the post-merge and range-sweep routes. Its refusal states that the mint was refused while the merge stands and directs recovery through a fetch followed by a sweep over the same range, or through a reviewed repair followed by a sweep whose after revision is the repairing commit. The contract covers ledger and snapshot inputs produced by supported signing and act routes; hand-edited carriers, alias spellings and sub-second timing windows are outside it.
Rationale 3% of the words changed
Suppressing a record without both a new re-attestationre-acceptance and equality to its approved copy would hide a later amendment, while a record an owneroperator row carries is moved, not hidden: it stays on the approval brief as drift and is named by the owner'soperator's item; treating a present unreadable carrier as absence would make the suppression decision unauditable. The later-writer arm accepts one bound rather than minting on every later copy of the registry: a routed traced cell restored between two acts is re-anchored by the later copy, as the snapshot already re-anchors any traced change without a verdict.

An act that both approves rows and re-attestsre-accepts rows, claimed either by two single-kind rows or by one combined sitting's per-kind tokens, merges when each half lies inside its claiming row's own kind scope, whether their rows are in one registry or different ones; an id under another combined kind authorizes neither half, a snapshot is WIDENED only when the complete acted set holds no approved or re-attestedre-accepted row in that registry identity, a row the act ledger names being placed in the registry its id's tier names whether or not the row remains in the live registry at the head, so a retirement authorizes its own registry's copy: every carrier path of an authorized registry, including a deleted obsolete carrier copy, is authorized, while an unauthorized registry's copy is WIDENED on every carrier path.
Method 4% of the words changed
Driven on real git repositories made from scaffolds. An adjudication lane claiming an amendment row scoped to one requirement, whose act re-attestsre-accepts two amended requirements, is refused at merge naming the one outside the scope; an act re-attestingre-accepting only the scoped row merges, and the same act claimed by a first-approvalfirst-acceptance row is refused naming the row, since that lane holds no re-attestationre-acceptance scope. A combined act across the same or different registries merges when each section acts only within its own kind scope and every copied registry has an acted row, including a ledger-only approval; a copied registry neither section moved is WIDENED. On a RELEASED rung, an act naming an unacceptedunrecorded verdict is refused by the verdict named, and its whole act, a first approval included, is refused. Each act permitted to merge in these cases carries branch bindings that judge every row it flips APPROVE and every row it re-attestsre-accepts CLARITY, or MEANING with the bless mark, written by _bind_branch; a named verdict must itself be accepted and authorize each row its act re-attestsre-accepts in the same way, and omitting --verdict does not waive the branch binding. On a RELEASED rung, an act re-attestingre-accepting a row that its accepted amendment verdict rules plain MEANING, or tags MEANING+BLESS and another way, is refused naming the row, through the backing check and through a named verdict alike. A combined act carrying one is refused whole. The same act under a MEANING+BLESS ruling merges. A first-approvalfirst-acceptance part that RETURNs its only judged row approves nothing, while its combined act may re-attestre-accept its amendment row. One act that approves a Drafted requirement and re-attestsre-accepts an amended one, claimed by a first-approvalfirst-acceptance row scoped to the first and an amendment row scoped to the second, merges; the same act whose amendment row is scoped to another requirement is refused naming the re-attestedre-accepted row. On a RELEASED rung, an act whose only re-attestationre-acceptance retires an Approved row the lane deleted, ruled by an accepted amendment verdict inside the amendment scope, merges with that registry's copy as its only copy. The same retirement on a held rung is refused by row. The re-attestationre-acceptance ledger reader refuses by name when either ledger side does not parse; acts already on trunk are not re-read. Every carrier path of an authorized registry, including a deleted obsolete carrier copy, is authorized, while an unauthorized registry's copy is WIDENED on every carrier path.

SR-181A spine edit that lowers the effective stage surfaces as a phase changere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall require, at authoring time, that any registry edit which drops the derived effective stage carry a Phase tag on every row it added or moved a stage-affecting cell on that is NOT the phase the settled work already stood in — a new (higher) phase, or an already-open lower one — except a decrease landing exactly on the DevStg-LLReqs to DevStg-Arch transition, which is within-phase decomposition rework and carries no such obligation.

Rationale

Realizes SN-004: an edit that regresses the spine's own derived readiness without opening a new phase is a gate advanced past what the tree actually shows, the false green SN-008 exists to refuse. Ruled in docs/plans/2026-08-21-stage-unification-plan.md §4 and the operator's answer §6.1: phase stays a pure function of the registries (no stored counter, alternative (ii) declined) — the decrease rule is an authoring-time check on the row tags themselves rather than a second phase concept that could drift against them, and `docs/stage` records the derived phase exactly as `docs/gate` did. The one exemption is deliberately narrow: the operator confirmed exactly the one-rung `DevStg-LLReqs -> DevStg-Arch` permutation (the permitted decomposition cycle), not a wider Arch-tier allowance, because a deep decomposition would otherwise run the phase counter up for churn that is not a scope regression. This row corrects a mis-trace: `derive_stage.phase_rule_findings` previously declared `Implements: SR-139`, crediting a requirement about approval authority (which tier an operator holds) with a realization edge from a function that states a different obligation entirely (a spine edit's own honesty about scope). The false edge is removed and this row states the obligation the function actually implements, and the function's declaration now points at it.

SR-186Proportionate requirement decompositionre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered requirements process shall require each additional child within a required tier to carry an independent decision or verification purpose, and record the stopping decision in the scoped decomposition record, while retaining the required SN-to-SR-to-LLR-to-TC tiers and linking real verification to the existing obligation.

Rationale

Carries SN-012's unowned granularity clause as a process requirement on what the delivered process requires and records. A child that only paraphrases a parent or duplicates another child's verification adds review and maintenance cost without an independent decision. The process records the stopping decision within the required spine; this row does not guarantee adopter behavior beyond that record, and it never permits omitting a required SN→SR→LLR→TC tier or replacing real verification with a count. It does not impose a row-count cap, deletion quota, or new machine gate. Existing process doctrine and the spine-authoring adjudicator questions are the source of the judgment, while mechanism-specific evidence remains with its current SR.

approved — re-acceptance owed
Detail 0% of the words changed
A sitting brief for a decomposition round carries every declared perspective question applicable to that round and asks the verdict to name one outcome for each perspective. The verdict's per-perspective outcome lines are neither row-ruling lines nor machine lines, so a verdict carrying them parses to the same rulings and judged rows as one without them. A decomposition round's sitting brief also carries a named stopping-boundary line, asking the verdict to state, for each retained chain, why further splitting would only paraphrase or duplicate; a round with no roster or no applicable perspective carries it beside its no-perspective line, because the stopping decision rests on no perspective. A stopping-boundary line is likewise neither a row-ruling line nor a machine line, and nothing checks for it: a retained chain with no stopping reason is a finding for the review of the verdict. A decomposition round judges a system requirement awaiting first approval or an approved stakeholder need whose text is amended; another judged set carries no perspective question and no stopping-boundary line. The applicable set combines each amended need with each need named by a system requirement the sitting judges, including an amended system requirement, widens each need by the authoring work item's declared tags, and evaluates each need alone. A first-approvalfirst-acceptance or amendment row a route mints records the declared tags of the work items that route names as its authors, and those tags stand in place of the row's own classification; a route naming no authoring work item records none, and the row widens by its own tags. Such a row minted from a minted row passes that record on, so the minted and in-lane sittings for one system requirement reach one perspective set wherever the authoring work item is named. Questions and the stopping-boundary line fill the perspective slot only when the sitting template declares it; a template without that slot composes unchanged. A sitting composed from several judgement kinds carries the questions and the stopping-boundary line once, after its last section, and says under which section the verdict writes those lines. Outside a decomposition round the roster is not read. An absent roster yields its no-perspective line, while an unreadable existing roster refuses a round's composition only when its template declares the perspective slot, and names the roster.

SR-189Each need resolves to the declared stakeholders whose outcome it isre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall resolve each stakeholder need's stakeholder references against the declared stakeholder list, and each stakeholder's party against the declared frame, reporting a need that names no stakeholder.

Rationale

A need with no named owner has nobody who can confirm it is still wanted, and a stakeholder's party is what lets the need's outcome be placed on the frame. The link lives on the need, pointing at the stakeholder, so the relation has one home; a short list beside the needs keeps the stakeholders where the rows citing them already are, rather than in a registry of their own. A stakeholder is not a review perspective: a stakeholder owns an outcome, while a perspective owns a question put to each decomposition, so no perspective becomes a stakeholder row.

SR-190A need's source pointer resolves to a document and anchorre-accept owed

Requirement

Where a stakeholder need records the document it was drawn from, the delivered harness shall resolve that pointer to an existing file and anchor.

Rationale

A need drawn from a longer document — an operator's statement of design constraints, an adopter's needs catalog — drifts from it unseen unless the need says where it came from. The need stays the canonical obligation and the document is its provenance, so the pointer takes a cell of its own instead of a place in the need's text, which is kept free of repository paths so a stakeholder can read it. A pointer that does not resolve is the same rot as a dead link, and fails the same way.

SR-193Each requirement cites its assumptions or records why it needs nonere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report each system requirement that neither cites the assumptions its argument relies on, names the sibling requirements that jointly deliver its needs, nor records why its own specification alone delivers its needs.

Rationale

An empty cell asserts nothing, so a requirement citing no assumption cannot be read as one that needs none: the absence is unknown, and only an explicit waiver says the system's own behavior is the outcome. A sibling requirement is governed system behavior rather than a premise about the world, while a requirement that contributes with siblings cannot truthfully claim its own specification alone delivers the need; joint delivery is therefore neither an assumption citation nor a coincident waiver. The need link stays on the requirement, because one interface serves several arguments and inheriting needs through an assumption would give a requirement the needs of an assumption it merely shares a seam with. Delivered-With states part of the requirement's delivery argument, so changing it changes the row's meaning and re-opens attestation; DA-Refs points to separately attested premises without rewriting that delivery claim, so changing a citation does not. Reporting rather than failing keeps the classification a worklist until the gate that relies on it is enabled.

SR-197A test case names the assumptions it can falsify in a field of its ownre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall accept a test case that names the assumptions its failure shows false in place of, or beside, the requirements and design rows it verifies, placing a test case that names only assumptions in every phase of the requirements that cite them.

Rationale

A test that can show an assumption false is not evidence about the system's behavior, and counting both in one field would merge the two obligations the argument separates: that the system does what its requirements say, and that what they say reaches the outcome. A separate reference keeps the verified-requirement join exactly what it was, and lets a test of an assumption stand alone where no requirement is its subject. Every reader that counts evidence has to make the same split, or two views of one test case disagree about what it proves. Phase follows the requirements that rely on the assumption, because an assumption has no phase of its own.

SR-198An observation test declares what it reads, how long its result holds, and how it samplesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report an observation test case that omits the inputs its judgment reads, its result lifetime or, where its failure shows an assumption false, its sampling policy, and refuse one declaring a lifetime shorter than seven days, an input path outside the repository, or a sampling policy outside the closed pair of sampled and monitored.

Rationale

An observation — a person reading a render, a critique of a rendered view, a measurement taken across an adopter's first week — cannot be rerun for every tree, so its result is trusted only while the state it judged is unchanged, and for a declared time. Declaring the inputs it reads is what lets a changed input make the result stale without a model call; the lifetime floor keeps a judgment from being demanded more often than it can honestly be taken. The author proposes the lifetime and the row's approval accepts it, because how fast a premise can change is a judgment about the world. A sampling model states how many samples are judged and what counts as a failing one, so a failed sample is recognizable as falsification evidence; a passed sample proves nothing beyond itself. Omissions are reported rather than refused so observation tests written before these cells existed keep passing on upgrade; the declarations are approved content because they state how the row's claim is kept current.

SR-199Observation results are recorded apart from their test casere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered process shall record each observation result apart from its test case, with its outcome, when it was observed, who or what observed it, when it expires and a digest of the inputs it judged.

Rationale

Keeping a result on the approved test case would mix what the test is with what it last found, and would force the row's re-acceptance after every sample. A result carries what it judged — the digest of the rows and artifacts its test case declares it reads — so a later change to those inputs makes it stale without a clock, and it carries an expiry so it cannot stand forever. One record serves assumption observations and the verdicts of inspection, critique and attestation tests alike, so all of them share one freshness rule. Automated tests need no such record: their results join the harness's tree-bound evidence record.

SR-202An accepted risk reopens on a failed sample or on any change to what it was accepted forre-accept owed

Requirement

When a sample for an assumption relied on under an accepted risk fails, or the text of the assumption or of a need it served when the risk was accepted changes after that acceptance, the delivered harness shall read the assumption as unproven until the risk is accepted again.

Rationale

A recorded accepted risk is a judgment about a particular assumption serving particular needs, so it cannot outlive a change to either, nor a sample showing the assumption failing. Binding the acceptance to the texts as they stood when it was made is what keeps a later, separate re-approval of a changed need from silently carrying the old risk forward. A clock would reopen it for no reason and teach readers to re-accept by reflex, so time alone never reopens it. Accepting again is a reviewed approval, like the first acceptance.

The delivered approval brief shall present each assumption and surrogate awaiting approval with the requirements citing it, the needs it serves, the crossings its outcome lands on, the test cases whose failure shows it false, and its falsifier.

SR-207An approval act refuses to carry drift it does not itself approvere-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall refuse to refresh a registry's acceptance record in an approval act while any row of that registry that the act neither approves nor re-accepts has approved text differing from its recorded copy.

Rationale

The recorded copy is the approver's asserted definition of the whole file, so refreshing it copies every row as it now stands. While any single approval in an act was enough to refresh the file, one row's approval silently blessed every other row's unreviewed edit. Refusing row by row keeps the copy to what someone saw, and it works for any number of tiers in one file, where splitting files or keying approvals by tier would each have needed a new approval identity through the whole approval path. Stakeholder needs stay outside this rule until their own text is compared with a recorded copy, which this row does not add.

SR-208Held-rung changes are refused before they landre-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared approval level holds a snapshotted registry's rung for an operator, the delivered harness shall refuse, before it lands on trunk, both a lane's approval claim that is not a CLARITY re-acceptance bound to the row's judged text and a marked autonomous commit outside a lane that moves a held status or makes a held approval claim.

Rationale

The approval level names the rungs an operator still approves, and an automated approval of the spine's own rows is already refused. The frame, assumption, surrogate and component registries carry status cells of their own that no automated path was stopped from changing, because the one setting that would stop it defaults to allowing. A policy that declares a rung operator-held without refusing the automated path is a claim, not a control. A lane can carry an approval into trunk even when no automated writer made its commit, and an autonomous commit outside a lane can make the same change; protecting only selected writers leaves the held state dependent on who delivered it. Binding the permitted re-acceptance to its judged text prevents a verdict about one text authorizing another, while leaving an unmarked reviewed trunk approval to its operator authority.

Method 1% of the words changed
Driven on real git repositories with the dial holding DevStg-Boundary. A lane whose commit flips a row into approval, adds it approved, moves its copy's approval cells or Status, or retires its approved copy is refused at landing naming the row, rung and dial; a Drafted sibling, demotion, below-approval move, traced-only copy move, released rung and example row pass. The same lane cases are exercised for a held stakeholder need, an ordinary lane, a coordinator lane, a re-claimed lane, a refresh merge and an admitted or non-admitted squash. The same change on a released rung merges. A registry missing from the rung map is held. An unreadable or unparseable live registry or copy is refused by name. A marked autonomous trunk commit that moves a held status or makes a held approval claim is refused by the hook and each loop writer; an unmarked plain trunk commit passes, and a marked commit inside a lane is judged at landing. The claim writer, the mint bookkeeping writer and the telemetry writer each refuse, before writing outside a lane, a tree that carries such a change; every handback commit, including the residue writer, runs the refusal outside a lane, while the handback residue writer inside a lane passes and its lane is judged at landing. The held set is every tier of the snapshotted registries; the assumptions registry is held at DevStg-Boundary and the needs file's stakeholder tier at DevStg-Needs. The dial is read at trunk HEAD for a landing and at the commit's parent for the marked arm, never from the working file and translating each legacy spelling silently. During a merge the hook step judges the staged result against its first parent, less each status a merged side already carries. The lane rider judges each lane commit after parent-first, and the slot's loop-lane held-status rung does not run. On a held tier, an adjudication act re-attestingre-accepting a row is refused unless its recorded verdict names that row as CLARITY; a MEANING verdict and an absent, unreadable or non-CLARITY verdict are refused by row; and a first draft is not re-attestedre-accepted under this allowance.

SR-209Every commit the loop makes carries a checked provenance trailerre-accept owed

Requirement

When a commit is made from a process the unattended loop started, or is merged in a lane the loop owns from the point the loop took that lane over, the delivered commit floor shall refuse it unless it carries a valid provenance trailer naming the loop and its session.

Rationale

A status change on an operator-held rung can be told apart from an operator's only if every loop-made commit says it is one. Without a floor that holds every loop commit to it, a trailer could appear on only some of the loop's commits and a missing one would prove nothing. Where a commit is made, the condition is who made it, not when: a person committing in another checkout while the loop runs is not the loop. Where a lane merges, the floor sees commits, not processes, so it reads whose lane it is from the commits and judges every commit of a loop lane, a person's included: there an unmarked commit the loop made cannot be told from a person's, and a person's commit belongs in the person's own lane. The commits made before the loop took a lane over are exempt, since nothing then could have marked them. Refusing the unmarked commit at the floor makes the mark total, which is what lets a later check treat its absence as meaningful. The floor where a commit is made is local and a determined bypass defeats it, which is why the merge re-checks a loop lane and the history check stands behind both.

SR-209 itself — no cell of this row changed

SN-RefsSN-029;SN-005
Boundary-RefsB-01;B-04
Hat-RefsSECURITY;UNATTENDED-OPS
AcceptanceCriteriaEvery process the loop starts carries a marker the commit floor reads, so a commit made from a loop-started process is known as the loop's; such a commit with no trailer, or with a malformed one, is refused naming the commit's subject; a commit made by a process the loop did not start needs no trailer and passes where it is made, even while the loop is running; the same validity rule, a trailer that is present and well-formed, applies wherever the commit floor runs. Where the floor judges a lane's commits at its merge, it reads whose lane it is from the commits: a lane is the loop's when its claim, or any commit one of the loop's own writers made in its range, carries the trailer. Every commit of a loop lane is then judged, whoever runs the merge, so a person's commit there must carry the trailer or move to the person's own lane; the commits before the lane's first trailer-carrying loop-writer commit are exempt from this check; a lane that is not the loop's is not judged. An attended re-claim recorded in the lane, a commit that changes nothing against its one parent, names that lane in the re-claim form, and carries no provenance trailer at all, ends the loop's window for the commits after it; a commit that fails any of those conditions is judged like any other; a later loop-writer commit re-opens the window.

SR-211Each boundary interface is bridged or coincidentre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report each interface realizing a boundary crossing that neither names the assumptions carrying its reading to an outcome nor records why its reading is the outcome.

Rationale

A requirement is testable only if the interface it is met at is defined or its reading is clearly assumed. The allocation is recorded on the interface, which is approved at the architecture rung where interfaces are, so an assumption approved earlier at the boundary rung is never edited to point at a seam approved later. The requirement a seam answers stays derived through the interface's owner, because stating it on the interface would give that relation a second home.

SR-215At a checkpoint, an unjudged, expired or triggered observation test is queued once for re-judgingre-accept owed

Requirement

When a work item merges, a release is prepared or a stage gate is checked, the delivered harness shall file one re-judge work item per due observation case: one with no result, one whose result expired, or one whose declared trigger fires after its work-item floor; with no declared trigger, a change to its declared inputs makes it due, subject to that floor. It keeps at most one open item per case, and reports each observation case that cites no written pass criteria as a warning.

Rationale

Judgements cost time and model calls and vary across sessions. Written pass criteria fixed before the first judgement make the pass reviewable. The closed-work floor and the declared trigger are cost limits the operator directed (the PERFORMANCE lens): no change or checkpoint makes an accepted judgement due again within the configured number of closed work items of its latest record, and a declared trigger replaces input changes with the change or checkpoint it names, so a judgement can stand on changes it never judged until a qualifying change or checkpoint meets the floor or its result expires. First judgement and expiry keep missing or old evidence from standing indefinitely.

RequirementWhen a work item merges, a release is prepared or a stage gate is checked, the delivered harness shall file one re-judge work item per due observation case: one with no result, one whose result expired, or one whose declared trigger fires after its work-item floor; with no declared trigger, a change to its declared inputs makes it due, subject to that floor. It keeps at most one open item per case, and reports each observation case that cites no written pass criteria as a warning.
AcceptanceCriteriaA case with no result is due at once, and a case whose result expired is due at once; neither waits for the floor. Otherwise a declared trigger (matching changed files, a change to a module tagged with the named component, release preparation, or a stage-gate check) makes a case due only once the configured number of closed work items has passed since its latest record was committed; a case may raise that number but not lower it. With no trigger, a change to its declared inputs makes it due, subject to the same floor; with neither a trigger nor inputs, only absence and expiry make it due. Inputs and policy are read at the checkpoint revision. An open re-judge item suppresses a second, and the decision runs no model. An observation case that cites no written pass criteria is reported as a warning, never a failure, including under strict checking.

The judging itself is the re-judge item's own.

`intake.py sweep --before <sha> --after <sha> --branch <lane> --merged WI-###[;WI-###]` runs intake_after_merge over the range with an outcomes map holding exactly the named rows: merged_outcomes reads each one's outcome from the one terminal folder holding its spec (complete, partial or cancelled), so the early-close dispositions, the clean-close spot checks and the drafts a merged adjudication row names in its Dispositions section are minted for those rows and no others, beside the range's diff triggers (the amendment and first-approvalfirst-acceptance rows) and the merge checkpoint's re-judge drafts at `--after`. `--merged` judges one merge, so _merged_shape_refusal refuses it without both range ends, when the two name one commit, and without `--branch`. The branch is the claim identity the Done-when check reads: a named row whose claim is under `active/<branch>/` at `--before` is checked against it, and one whose claim is not there gets one stderr line naming the row, the branch and why the check did not run; `--branch` names the mint commit either way, and a range or history sweep hands the check no claim identity. A named row in no terminal folder, or in more than one, refuses the whole sweep by name and mints nothing. `--merged` and `--with-terminal` are mutually exclusive; the range shape without either still judges no close, and the bare sweep still judges every close on file. Idempotent by the mint's exact-title dedup, like every sweep.

SR-217A requirement implemented before its test cases were approved is reportedre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report each system requirement approved after the project's declared starting point whose implementation has landed on trunk while any of its test cases was not yet approved for it, reading the order from the committed history.

Rationale

Tests written after the code tend to describe what the code does rather than what was required, so the order is the evidence that a passing run means the requirement is met. The stage ladder puts test cases before implementation for a project as a whole, but not requirement by requirement, and the committed history is the one record of order that no cell can restate after the fact. Code declaring which requirement or design row it implements is the one event that marks an implementation landing. A requirement's approval is its entry into scope, so judging only requirements approved after a declared starting point keeps a project that adopts the rule from being judged on history written before it; a project that declares none is judged whole. A test case is evidence for a requirement only once it is approved while it names that requirement: dated from its own approval alone, a test case approved for something else could be re-pointed at code already written and lend it an order it never had. A test case not yet approved is the same gap at its widest, since its passing run shows only that the code does what unapproved text says; the report names it with a warning rather than withholding the result, which a reviewer can still weigh.

SR-222Every model session is recorded in one usage record, whichever provider CLI serves itre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall record every model session it launches, whichever provider command-line runner serves it, in one usage record: token usage under a published usage vocabulary pinned to a named revision, input counted inclusive of cached input, fresh input derived by one formula, the runner's raw usage kept verbatim, the route's provider filled from its roster row for every routed call, the runner named, the vocabulary's gen_ai.provider.name holding the runner's default provider for claude and codex and empty for any other runner, with runner reconfiguration to another provider not detected, and the context occupancy of the session's latest request kept apart from its billed tokens; for a runner other than claude, codex and opencode, the runner name is left empty, and so is every count or raw usage the loop cannot read from the runner's output.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-026 asks that the operator can configure several model families and route work among them per job and capability level; it does not name a usage record, so this obligation arrives through two lenses rather than through the need's text. The performance lens listens for measurements that cannot be compared, or are unavailable, being read as a reliable total: routing among families is a cost and quality choice, and the choice is blind when one family's calls record their usage and another's do not, or when the runners disagree on what "input tokens" means (two count cached input apart from input, one counts it inside), so one column would hold two incompatible numbers. The consistency lens listens for readers disagreeing after a one-sided change: when each launching role keeps its own launch and logging path, a usage fix lands in one path and not the others. A published vocabulary avoids inventing a log format for a problem that is not novel; because it has no tagged release, the record pins the exact revision it follows. The raw usage is kept verbatim so a mapping later found wrong is re-derived rather than lost. Occupancy is kept apart from billed tokens because they answer different questions: billed tokens are summed over every request the session made, while how full a context is depends on the latest request alone, and a session reset that read the first as the second would fire on sessions that are nowhere near full. A runner who… [376 more chars — read the registry row]

The consistency lens listens for readers disagreeing after a one-sided change: when each launching role keeps its own launch and logging path, a usage fix lands in one path and not the others. The raw usage is kept verbatim so a mapping later found wrong is re-derived rather than lost. Fed back to the need: SN-026's acceptance could name comparable per-family usage as what makes routing among families an informed choice; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-225A delegated run closes with a record of the calls it made, where the declared dial asks for onere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall keep the operator's verdict on each delegated decision coupled to the work that acts on it and each delegated run to its record: whatever the declared decision-recording dial, reporting without refusing a record entry that omits a required disclosure field or leaves one blank, listing each entry the operator has not yet seen and each overruled entry with the open work that carries it, and refusing an overrule unless its transition change files or amends open work that cites the entry; and, where that dial asks for a record, refusing to integrate a closing lane whose record is absent, naming where it belongs.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-029 asks that a run released to automation get as far as it honestly can, and that an approval it makes on a released tier leave a record naming who made it; it does not name the other calls a delegated run makes on the operator's behalf, the ones too settled to hold the run for and not settled enough to be history, so this obligation arrives through the unattended-operations lens rather than through the need's text. A call nobody is told about is the failure that lens listens for: it pages nobody, and a run that looks green is green partly because nothing looked at what it chose. Required fields and a close refusal make that record durable rather than an instruction that can be omitted. The obligation is keyed to a dial because how much of the operator's reading a run may claim is the operator's to set; it ships off, so a repository owes nothing until its owner asks. Every close owes the record, a partial close included, because every delegated run closes with one; a lane the machinery closed with no session present is refused too, and that refusal is a hold for a person to write the record rather than a strand. A malformed entry is reported rather than refused, because the record is there and readable and a refusal would hold finished work for a reporting defect. A decision is an already selected direction, so the operator either confirms it or overrules it; approval would falsely imply a new selection. A closed verdict makes that … [1013 more chars — read the registry row]

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that a configured agent implement toward the vision with no human curating what comes next; it does not name retaining a session, so this obligation arrives through three lenses rather than through the need's text. The performance lens listens for an operating-cost risk left unassessed: a run that spins a fresh adjudicator for every small work item reloads the spine on each call, and the usage record makes that cost visible, while resuming a session by id uses the provider's prompt cache. The unattended-operations lens listens for a silent degrade: a retained session that has filled, judges under changed rules, or is started in a home whose sign-in cannot be read degrades every later judgement with nothing paging anyone; a coordinator route that bypasses the retained operation repeats that cost and loses the state the loop preserves. One composition keeps both routes under the same drain and lease rules. The integrity lens listens for a durable artifact updated in place without an all-or-nothing guarantee and for a claim nothing can reclaim: two calls resuming one transcript at once corrupt it, so one call at a time holds a session, under a hold that expires when its holder is gone. Refusing an unreadable or absent sign-in before that hold prevents a failed retained launch from changing state or escaping into a person's default home. Retiring only when no work the session has a stake in is pending keeps a review, rework and … [503 more chars — read the registry row]

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that a configured agent implement toward the vision with no human curating what comes next; it does not name retaining a session, so this obligation arrives through three lenses rather than through the need's text. The performance lens listens for an operating-cost risk left unassessed: a run that spins a fresh adjudicator for every small work item reloads the spine on each call, and the usage record makes that cost visible, while resuming a session by id uses the provider's prompt cache. The unattended-operations lens listens for a silent degrade: a retained session that has filled, judges under changed rules, or is started in a home whose sign-in cannot be read degrades every later judgement with nothing paging anyone; a coordinator route that bypasses the retained operation repeats that cost and loses the state the loop preserves. One composition keeps both routes under the same drain and lease rules. The integrity lens listens for a durable artifact updated in place without an all-or-nothing guarantee and for a claim nothing can reclaim: two calls resuming one transcript at once corrupt it, so one call at a time holds a session, under a hold that expires when its holder is gone. Refusing an unreadable or absent sign-in before that hold prevents a failed retained launch from changing state or escaping into a person's default home. Retiring only when no work the session has a stake in is pending keeps a review, rework and re-review round trip in one session; a session is retained as a transcript a bounded process replays, never as a long-lived process, so an unattended run still cannot wait on a prompt. The dial is keyed off because turning it on is the owner'soperator's decision once the layer has been verified where it runs. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name bounded operating cost per judgement as part of what lets a run proceed with no human curating it; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

The publisher then applies its marker under store_lock within APPLY_WAIT, or it stands for the next locked read. A failed publication raises OSError and leaves no marker. A release drops its publisher's lease; a retire retires only the live session and generation it names and drops a lease only when its publisher holds it; a bookkeep lands under _landing's rule, and one that no longer lands releases its holder's lease if still held. Every marker therefore takes effect at most once: a call's marker only while its publisher's lease stands, and a scope retirement only on the live session and generation it names, so a marker left by a failed delete is inert on a later locked or lockless read. A ping whose launch raised TreeNotEnded hands it with the finished call to the dispatcher's thread, and the tick that sees it, or the run's end, raises it: over a clean trunk after recording the call, a failure to record riding as its context; over a dirty trunk unrecorded, the hold not deferring it. Any other failure of the ping is recorded as an ERROR call and the run continues. REVIEW. reviewer_dials is the one reader of the reviewer table: it reads a 0..100 non-boolean integer reset percent and persisted final reviewer only while that percent is positive; absent, unreadable, unparseable or ill-typed settings read as off and fresh. review_retention returns ReviewRetention(scope, stage, pin): it returns no scope for a non-review phase, no claim base, or an off review dial; a narrow round uses the iteration stage; a full round retires live iteration records through retire markers, which take effect for the lockless pin at once and are applied by the next locked read, and is unretained when fresh or uses the final stage when persisted. scoped_route pins a live record after folding its pending markers for the settled scope; unavailable pins fall through ordinary selection. The loop stores scope, stage and once-resolved review template content in routing state, and passes scope and that content only for a review keep.
Rationale 0% of the words changed
Retention is one more thing a call does, not a second launch path, so resume, occupancy, reset and keep-warm all go through act and record, and the rules and the store sit in their own module beside the service rather than in the roles. The layer ships off because turning it on is the owner'soperator's decision after it has been verified on the machine it runs on, and at the off dial the launch is exactly a fresh session's. The lock and the lease exist because a lane's worker and the dispatcher both reach the one store and the one transcript: a torn record or two calls resuming one session at once corrupts the state every later judgement reads. The clear point reads the queue and the lanes rather than the item alone because a draining session that retires while a successor of its own verdict is still queued breaks the round trip the layer exists for. The keep-warm ping is off the dispatcher's thread so a slow ping cannot stall the merges, and its record is on it so its commit is serialised with them. A qualified account home keeps its retained transcript out of a person's own sessions, while an unqualified entry retains in its ambient launch environment; a long-lived credential is read only for the launch that needs it, so no retained record becomes a credential store. The review class uses the existing store, lease and service homes rather than a copy; scoped identity keeps its records distinct from adjudicator records and preserves empty-scope filenames.

PREPARATION. prepare_launch reads no registry: from that row and the selected entry account it derives family, template, model, tier, route environment, account environment, account home and launch credential. A token account is signed-in exactly when the file its token_file_variable names is present, readable and nonempty; its probe runs no command. A login-account home resolves without being created. For a login account home, only documented command-run pairs count: Codex accepts exactly one Logged in using <method> line at exit 0 or exactly Not logged in at exit 1, apart from blank lines and its PATH-alias warning; Claude without a token accepts exactly one JSON object with boolean loggedIn true at exit 0 or false at exit 1; another answer, failure or timeout is unknown. An absent, unreadable or empty token file refuses before a lease, naming the declared variable and the setup step but never its path or value. refuse_competing checks every declared account: its route or account environment may not declare a credential source ranked above its account home; a token account also may not declare its token variable, and only a token account’s template may not carry --bare; names compare under platform case rules; settings-file credential sources are outside this boundary. compose_env builds the launch environment by removing names the launch sets and competing credential names, then applying route pairs, account pairs, home and token as the launch's one environment credential. Prepared carries the template's first token after normal substitution, resolved once to an absolute executable on that environment's PATH; failure refuses before a lease and names the runner and declared or ambient PATH. cli_version and the retained launch run that executable; _as_prepared makes act launch and account the selected row rather than caller copies. probe_env composes the prepared environment with the launch credential withheld. OUTPUT. act redacts each verbatim occurrence of the credential value from physical output lines and captured stream before result, usage, logs or records consume it; escaped, encoded and line-split representations are outside that bound. For a qualified OpenCode account, the environment starts from its declared platform and network-transport base plus kit-owned names, then route pairs, account pairs and home, never ambient environment; OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT is refused. No registry reread, fallback or automatic sign-in occurs. AdjudicationRequest also carries scope and account. governing_templates receives the request role: for REVIEW it returns the once-resolved reviewer template text used by the brief, and for ADJUDICATE it keeps the retained-class identity; adjudication_keep passes that role. The governing identity of a retained set holding amendment, first-approval,first-acceptance, or combined also covers the act brief, by its wired override text when present and otherwise by its shipped text.
Rationale 1% of the words changed
A coordinator route that retained independently would duplicate the request composition, state path and account-home policy, so drift in either route could resume a different session or record a different governing input. The shared request is the single join before keep planning. A missing or indeterminate account sign-in cannot safely be treated as a fresh launch: that would bypass the retained home and leave a session record whose authentication context is unknown. Reading the credential at launch rather than retaining it makes each launch reflect the owner'soperator's current provision without exposing the value in repository state. Reading an ordinary home without creating it makes refusal leave no new state.

SR-228Held-rung CLARITY re-acceptancere-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared approval level holds a tier for an operator, the delivered loop shall permit an independent adjudication to re-accept an approved amended row only when its verdict rules that amendment CLARITY.

Rationale

SN-029 delegates review on released tiers without skipping it, but an approved row whose wording is clarified on a held tier remains anchored to a signature the operator already gave. Treating that unchanged meaning as a new approval would strand every clarification with the operator; treating a meaning change the same way would carry a signature onto text the operator did not read. The verdict boundary keeps those alternatives separate: only the independent judgement that the signature still describes the row permits re-acceptance, while a meaning change remains the operator's decision.

Method 1% of the words changed
Driven on real git repositories with the dial holding DevStg-Boundary. A lane whose commit flips a row into approval, adds it approved, moves its copy's approval cells or Status, or retires its approved copy is refused at landing naming the row, rung and dial; a Drafted sibling, demotion, below-approval move, traced-only copy move, released rung and example row pass. The same lane cases are exercised for a held stakeholder need, an ordinary lane, a coordinator lane, a re-claimed lane, a refresh merge and an admitted or non-admitted squash. The same change on a released rung merges. A registry missing from the rung map is held. An unreadable or unparseable live registry or copy is refused by name. A marked autonomous trunk commit that moves a held status or makes a held approval claim is refused by the hook and each loop writer; an unmarked plain trunk commit passes, and a marked commit inside a lane is judged at landing. The claim writer, the mint bookkeeping writer and the telemetry writer each refuse, before writing outside a lane, a tree that carries such a change; every handback commit, including the residue writer, runs the refusal outside a lane, while the handback residue writer inside a lane passes and its lane is judged at landing. The held set is every tier of the snapshotted registries; the assumptions registry is held at DevStg-Boundary and the needs file's stakeholder tier at DevStg-Needs. The dial is read at trunk HEAD for a landing and at the commit's parent for the marked arm, never from the working file and translating each legacy spelling silently. During a merge the hook step judges the staged result against its first parent, less each status a merged side already carries. The lane rider judges each lane commit after parent-first, and the slot's loop-lane held-status rung does not run. On a held tier, an adjudication act re-attestingre-accepting a row is refused unless its recorded verdict names that row as CLARITY; a MEANING verdict and an absent, unreadable or non-CLARITY verdict are refused by row; and a first draft is not re-attestedre-accepted under this allowance.

Method 4% of the words changed
Driven on real git repositories made from scaffolds. An adjudication lane claiming an amendment row scoped to one requirement, whose act re-attestsre-accepts two amended requirements, is refused at merge naming the one outside the scope; an act re-attestingre-accepting only the scoped row merges, and the same act claimed by a first-approvalfirst-acceptance row is refused naming the row, since that lane holds no re-attestationre-acceptance scope. A combined act across the same or different registries merges when each section acts only within its own kind scope and every copied registry has an acted row, including a ledger-only approval; a copied registry neither section moved is WIDENED. On a RELEASED rung, an act naming an unacceptedunrecorded verdict is refused by the verdict named, and its whole act, a first approval included, is refused. Each act permitted to merge in these cases carries branch bindings that judge every row it flips APPROVE and every row it re-attestsre-accepts CLARITY, or MEANING with the bless mark, written by _bind_branch; a named verdict must itself be accepted and authorize each row its act re-attestsre-accepts in the same way, and omitting --verdict does not waive the branch binding. On a RELEASED rung, an act re-attestingre-accepting a row that its accepted amendment verdict rules plain MEANING, or tags MEANING+BLESS and another way, is refused naming the row, through the backing check and through a named verdict alike. A combined act carrying one is refused whole. The same act under a MEANING+BLESS ruling merges. A first-approvalfirst-acceptance part that RETURNs its only judged row approves nothing, while its combined act may re-attestre-accept its amendment row. One act that approves a Drafted requirement and re-attestsre-accepts an amended one, claimed by a first-approvalfirst-acceptance row scoped to the first and an amendment row scoped to the second, merges; the same act whose amendment row is scoped to another requirement is refused naming the re-attestedre-accepted row. On a RELEASED rung, an act whose only re-attestationre-acceptance retires an Approved row the lane deleted, ruled by an accepted amendment verdict inside the amendment scope, merges with that registry's copy as its only copy. The same retirement on a held rung is refused by row. The re-attestationre-acceptance ledger reader refuses by name when either ledger side does not parse; acts already on trunk are not re-read. Every carrier path of an authorized registry, including a deleted obsolete carrier copy, is authorized, while an unauthorized registry's copy is WIDENED on every carrier path.

SR-229Coordinator claim admission respects a blackout pausere-accept owed

Requirement

Where a blackout window is armed, the delivered work-item admission shall refuse a new claim inside that window on every route at any context-guard dial; outside a blackout window, where the declared coordinator context guard is enabled, it admits a coordinator claim only from the current lease holder while that holder's context drain is not latched, the drain latching once the holder's context occupancy reaches the declared threshold and holding across compaction and resume until the operator records a clear or a release, the holder records a hand-back naming its handoff, or a relaunched successor takes the lease.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 asks that a declared pause stop claiming and drain what is already in flight, and that recovery never double-assign work; it does not name the coordinating session's own context, so this obligation arrives through two lenses rather than through the need's text. The unattended-operations lens listens for a silent degrade: a coordinator whose context has crossed its declared limit keeps claiming after compaction has degraded the context it needs to close the work it already holds, and nothing pages anyone. The integrity lens listens for a recovery path written only for the unattended run when the same corruption is reachable attended, and for a claim nothing can reclaim once its holder is gone: a retained adjudicator session already drains on occupancy while the attended coordinator does not, and a second or missing holder leaves claim authority ambiguous, so one lease names the coordinator and only the operator's recorded release frees a lease whose holder has gone. A latched single-holder admission boundary was chosen over a one-time event observation because every claim must remain protected when an event is missed or the transcript later reports a lower reading. Fed back to the need: SN-027's acceptance could name the coordinating session's own capacity as a declared reason to stop claiming and drain; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

The unattended dispatcher's own admission remains available without consulting this guard. guard_config reads the declared coordinator threshold and window: a non-positive, out-of-range or malformed threshold is off and a malformed window reads as the default. read_occupancy reads the newest valid assistant usage after the live transcript branch's latest compaction boundary, never a sidechain record, counting input and cached input; a record whose usage is malformed, partial or zero is skipped, and no valid usage reads as unknown, never zero. A primary-checkout lease names one coordinator session and its transcript. take refuses another holder; release frees the lease and clear unlatches it, each requiring and recording the owner'soperator's reason; hand_back accepts only the holder session and a handoff carrying a session prompt, frees the lease, and records the handoff; it refuses another or unnamed caller, whatever handoff it names, while naming the owner'soperator's release; it refuses the holder's own pending relaunch request, while a previous holder's request does not block it and is left for session_end's foreign-request refusal; with the guard off it returns before reading or writing. Elapsed time never transfers ownership. on_session_start installs a session as holder, unlatched, only when it presents the successor token the holder's exit wrote into the lease, and restates a latched drain to the holder's own resumed start. Only the holder's own hook payload on the holder's transcript is measured, never a subagent's. latch_reading latches drain when the unrounded reading reaches the threshold and retains it through lower readings, compaction and resume; it ends only through the owner's clear, the owner'soperator's release, the holder's hand-back, or a successor take. window_refusal runs before the dial on every claim route, including the dispatcher, naming the UTC end; the dispatcher remains exempt only from the context guard. claim_refusal identifies the claimant by the session id the agent CLI exports to its tool processes (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID), refuses with no lease held or a claimant that is not the holder, and reads and latches the holder's transcript itself, so a refusal never depends on a hook having run; a claim holding the dispatch lock never calls it. While a window is armed hooks act at every dial and deny the closed list of the main session's Agent call, SendMessage call, Bash/PowerShell model-CLI command word, and a Bash/PowerShell line unreadable only because of an unclosed single quote, unclosed double quote, unclosed POSIX dollar quote, unclosed POSIX backtick substitution, unclosed dollar-parenthesis substitution, or unclosed PowerShell here-string. One quote-aware shell reading per dialect reads quoted values as the shell does, and treats quoted separators, comments and here-document and here-string bodies as data. It finds the model-CLI command word after leading variable assignments, the timeout and env prefixes, the shell's reserved words, the chain operators and the call operator, and in substitutions written in the line or inside double quotes. It reads a PowerShell assignment to a variable as running its right-hand command, while a quoted or variable right-hand value stays data. A form outside this list gets no dedicated recognition: it may incidentally match this reading, and carries no guarantee either way. window_check exits nonzero inside an armed window. At every SessionStart inside a window, hooks inject the blackout close-down instruction; each main session's monitored events inject it at that session's first monitored event in the window and every twentieth thereafter, counted per session per window: bring each open lane to its pause point, using a wrap-up adjudication for an active claim where needed; write the handoff naming each lane and its next obligation; request no relaunch; and end the session. Hook responses inject the latch instruction once and bounded reminders thereafter; inside a blackout window the latch is still recorded, but the blackout close-down, which requests no relaunch, is injected in its place. PreCompact records trigger, occupancy and latch/request state; classify_compaction reports missed-threshold, manual and during-drain cases. Before recording a holder, the lease take refuses an inactive commit floor and records no holder. After identifying a session, the lease take first reads the guard hooks' state and records no holder unless it reads none or on, or a terminal consent installs them and the re-read reads on; without a terminal at absent, or at occupied, it refuses naming the consent step or the hooks to move.
