SR-230Coordinator successor at session exit outside a blackout pausere-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared coordinator context guard is enabled, when the coordinator lease holder that has requested a relaunch from its handoff ends its session outside an armed blackout window, the delivered coordination support shall start exactly one successor session from that handoff; inside the window it cancels the pending request and leave resumption to the operator.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 asks that claiming drain what is already in flight and that a crash at any lifecycle boundary recover without double-assignment; it does not name a coordinating session handing over to its successor, so this obligation arrives through the integrity lens rather than through the need's text. That lens asks what the next reader finds when a holder is gone: a close-out that loses its handoff strands the next coordinator, and one that can launch twice creates competing claim authority. An atomic, owned request consumed once was chosen over treating every session-end event as a relaunch because clear and resume do not end the coordinator and a failed launch must remain recoverable. Fed back to the need: SN-027's acceptance could name an orderly handover of the coordinating role as part of a drain; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

RationaleA DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 asks that claiming drain what is already in flight and that a crash at any lifecycle boundary recover without double-assignment; it does not name a coordinating session handing over to its successor, so this obligation arrives through the integrity lens rather than through the need's text. That lens asks what the next reader finds when a holder is gone: a close-out that loses its handoff strands the next coordinator, and one that can launch twice creates competing claim authority. An atomic, owned request consumed once was chosen over treating every session-end event as a relaunch because clear and resume do not end the coordinator and a failed launch must remain recoverable. AcceptanceCriteriaWith the guard off, no exit launches anything. Outside an armed blackout window, a request from the holder for an existing handoff launches once at an exit in the declared repository and starts from that handoff. Inside the window, no relaunch is requested or launched, and a pending request at the holder's exit is cancelled and recorded as blackout. Clear, resume, a non-holder, a subagent and a foreign request launch nothing; concurrent exit handling consumes one request once; and a launch that fails for any reason restores the request.

session_prompt extracts the one fenced session prompt from a handoff, preserving headings inside that fence as prompt text. request_relaunch refuses inside a blackout window and otherwise accepts only the lease holder and an existing handoff, then writes a same-session request atomically. The hook's on_blackout SessionEnd dispatch calls blackout_session_end to cancel a pending request and record blackout inside a window; otherwise session_end acts only for a true exit by that holder in its declared repository, rejects a foreign request, and atomically renames one request to acquire it and holds the store lock from that acquisition until the launch is confirmed or the request restored, so restoration never waits on the lock. It writes a fresh successor token into the lease and the handoff prompt to a file, invokes the platform launcher detached in the declared root with that file and token, and on any failure before launch confirmation restores the request and removes the successor token and the prompt file. launch_command selects the Windows or POSIX launcher; launch_detached waits through its grace period and confirms only a still-running launcher or one that exits zero. Each launcher enters the declared root, resolves one interpreter by running its virtual-environment candidate followed by the candidates from its dev-setup's ordinary runtime search, and takes the first that reports Python 3.11 or later as its executable path; it exits nonzero with guidance when none resolves, runs window_check on that interpreter, exports the token as PT_COORDINATOR_TAKE for the successor's SessionStart take, and starts claude with the prompt as one argument: the POSIX one in a new terminal, the Windows one through exec_claude, which invokes claude with the extracted prompt. main dispatches the guard operations; reopening a session with the context latch still set needs the owneroperator recorded clear.

SR-231Coordinator adjudication enters from a claimed lane and accepts only its current verdictre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator adjudication entry point shall, regardless of the declared adjudicator retention dial, run only from a claimed lane worktree and read success only from a verdict that its own call wrote within that call's deadline. From a claimed lane, it takes only an act an accepted current verdict authorizes. The verdict, reservation, and deadline obligations stated first apply to the judging turn; the act turn's success is the completion contract stated in the acceptance criteria.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that a configured agent progress without a human curating what comes next; it does not state the entry boundary for an adjudication the coordinator starts, so this obligation arrives through two lenses. The unattended-operations lens listens for a run whose telemetry lands on trunk instead of the claimed work it judges, leaving a later reader unable to recover its work item context. The integrity lens listens for stale evidence being accepted as this call's success: a verdict left by an earlier or overdue call can make an unsuccessful current call look valid. A lane-local call that owns a fresh verdict reservation was chosen over trusting a caller-supplied path or a shared trunk record, because both leave the evidence's author and time ambiguous. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name attributable, current adjudication evidence as part of unattended progress; until it does, this row is derived and says so. An act is authorized only by an accepted, committed verdict, so it cannot substitute later work for the judgement that authorized it.

AcceptanceCriteriaAt every retention-dial value, a coordinator adjudication from the primary checkout, an unclaimed worktree or outside a repository refuses before launch; a valid claimed lane exclusively reserves a new verdict path and only one concurrent call can claim it; a successful call returns success only for a valid verdict it wrote before its deadline; and a failed, timed-out, missing or invalid verdict never returns success. From a claimed lane, a later adjudicator turn takes the act a recorded verdict authorizes from the lane head; before launch it refuses an unrecorded verdict, one owing no act, a verdict that judged a row in an unexplained state, or uncommitted lane changes, naming the relevant input. The turn reserves no verdict, writes no binding or outcome, is retained only where the verdict class is retained, and succeeds only when its call succeeds, every authorized act is taken, and verdict records remain unchanged. The reservation and verdict-success conditions stated first apply to the judging turn.

Detail 1% of the words changed
From ana acceptedrecorded verdict and its binding as committed at a revision, the act assembler derives every authorized act that the revision's committed registries and records do not carry in full. A first-approvalfirst-acceptance APPROVE act is derived only on a released rung; an amendment CLARITY act is derived on either rung with the verdict named when a listed row is held; an amendment MEANING act is derived only from a bless-marked row on a released rung. RETURN, unmarked or held MEANING, held APPROVE and Done-when verdict parts derive no act. Each authorized row is owed or taken by its committed status and whole-row recorded copy; any unrecognized state or unmatched tier refuses the whole derivation naming the row. An uncommitted, unbound, non-accepted or invalid verdict, a class deriving no act, a verdict with no remaining authorized act, or an approval without an approval record refuses the whole derivation naming why. The derived acts list amendment before first approval, and their brief is filled in full or not at all. At a revision, the later-act derivation reports the acts a verdict still owes or its refusal, and reports no outstanding act only when every authorized act is taken. It identifies the retained class from an accepted actable verdict binding. A re-attestre-accept of a row absent from the committed registries is a retirement: it is owed while its recorded copy holds the row and taken once the copy does not; on a held rung it derives no act. A first approval of an absent row is inconsistent and refuses naming the row. Which rows a verdict authorizes, a MEANING row only with its bless mark, is read from the one reader the merge's backing check also reads, and each authorized row's act from the one held-rung act policy that also informs the judging brief.

Expected 1% of the words changed
The bless mark reads MEANING to every rulings reader, and only an unambiguous marked row is blessed. From ana acceptedrecorded verdict and its binding as committed at a revision, the act assembler derives every authorized act that the revision's committed registries and records do not carry in full. Each authorized row is owed or taken by its committed status and whole-row recorded copy; any unrecognized state or unmatched tier refuses the whole derivation naming the row. An uncommitted, unbound, non-accepted or invalid verdict, a class deriving no act, a verdict with no remaining authorized act, or an approval without an approval record refuses the whole derivation naming why. The derived acts list amendment before first approval, and their brief is filled in full or not at all. A re-attestre-accept of a row absent from the committed registries is a retirement: it is owed while its recorded copy holds the row and taken once the copy does not; on a held rung it derives no act. A first approval of an absent row is inconsistent and refuses naming the row. Each row's act follows the held-rung policy that also informs the judging brief, with the bless mark as the added condition for a released-rung MEANING row.

Retire an approved row ruled CLARITY beside a first approval in the same registry and assert that the retirement is listed with the re-attestationsre-acceptances and that taking the listed acts through the snapshot writer leaves nothing owed; assert a held-rung retirement derives no act; assert a first approval of an absent row, no approval record, a row no compared tier holds, and a verdict outside the root each refuse naming why. Pin each row's act arm against the held-rung policy for every ruling and rung the verdict grammar admits, with and without the bless mark.

SR-232Combined adjudication preserves each requested judgementre-accept owed

Requirement

Where one lane checkpoint requests several declared adjudication kinds, the delivered adjudication content shall present and validate one sitting that preserves each kind's own scope, evidence and decision grammar.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks for unattended progress but does not require one sitting to carry several judgements. The unattended-operations lens catches a green checkpoint where a requested kind was never judged; the integrity-recoverability lens catches a partial write where one kind acts while another section refuses. A composed sitting was chosen so each judgement remains independently checkable while sharing its checkpoint. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name bounded, attributable checkpoint adjudication; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

A combined class accepts only amendment:<id>, first-approval:<id>first-acceptance:<id> and done-when:<id> Adjudicates tokens; it composes each named class through compose with that section's verdict path in fixed amendment, first-approval,first-acceptance, done-when order, and refuses whole if any section cannot compose. One parser reads machine lines one physical line at a time: every line whose first token is a machine keyword counts, complete or not, so a bare, split, bad-label or field-missing line invalidates. The same module's review_line is the one reader of a review VERDICT line: exactly one case-insensitive VERDICT keyword line is accepted only as `VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`; the filing boundary refuses every other form and the merge reader treats it as no verdict. A combined sitting names exactly the kinds bound at reservation in <verdict>.requested, has exactly one kind-form lower-case section per bound kind and none other, and has across the whole file exactly one complete line per bound kind and one SITTING line, and no line for another kind; a single-kind verdict has no kind-form section and exactly one complete line for its kind. One binding records pending before either route calls: the coordinator entry point binds the request exclusively at reservation, and the loop binds its composed request at composition; write_binding is its one writer and record_outcome its one route recorder and commit path, returning its `(outcome, why)` decision and recording accepted only when call_succeeded has derived exit 0, no timeout and no reported error result, and validation passes. A dispute binding also records the findings file its composed brief names. It is written by the one writer in the same call as the requested ids, on either route. The outcome rewrite carries it unchanged, as it carries the identity cell. A brief that names none binds none, which every reader reads as absent. call_succeeded is derived once and shared by both routes; a failed call is recorded failed without its verdict being read, and the loop consumes that same why as its completion obligation. The coordinator validates its pending binding before recording its outcome, while the loop records against the kinds read back from its bound request; later consumers use the accepted-verdictrecorded-verdict reader, which returns only an accepted, bound, valid verdict and each part's row rulings. Every row an adjudication merge act flips needs an APPROVE ruling in an accepted first-approvalfirst-acceptance part, and every row it re-attestsre-accepts needs a CLARITY ruling, or a MEANING ruling carrying the bless mark, in an accepted amendment part among the branch's own bindings, whether or not the act names a verdict; ana acceptedrecorded verdict over other rows authorizes nothing, and a named verdict must authorize each row its act re-attestsre-accepts in the same way. Failed, pending, unbound or other-class verdicts cover nothing. Ordinary and mixed lanes consume the same claimed-row reader at the merge: raw scope parsing, the complete acted set including ledger-only approvals, and the route’s normalized brief cannot give one consumer authority another does not see. Token and section parsing are shared by composition, validation, act scopes and merge-time minting; the class is routed and retainable through BRIEF_PROMPTS. An amendment verdict's `- [MEANING+BLESS]` row tag reads MEANING to every rulings reader, and a dedicated reader returns only rows so marked, treating a row without the mark or also tagged plain MEANING or CLARITY as not blessed. One reader of the rows ana acceptedrecorded verdict authorizes, a MEANING row only when so marked, serves both the merge and the act assembler.

Expected 1% of the words changed
The bless mark reads MEANING to every rulings reader, and only an unambiguous marked row is blessed. From ana acceptedrecorded verdict and its binding as committed at a revision, the act assembler derives every authorized act that the revision's committed registries and records do not carry in full. Each authorized row is owed or taken by its committed status and whole-row recorded copy; any unrecognized state or unmatched tier refuses the whole derivation naming the row. An uncommitted, unbound, non-accepted or invalid verdict, a class deriving no act, a verdict with no remaining authorized act, or an approval without an approval record refuses the whole derivation naming why. The derived acts list amendment before first approval, and their brief is filled in full or not at all. A re-attestre-accept of a row absent from the committed registries is a retirement: it is owed while its recorded copy holds the row and taken once the copy does not; on a held rung it derives no act. A first approval of an absent row is inconsistent and refuses naming the row. Each row's act follows the held-rung policy that also informs the judging brief, with the bless mark as the added condition for a released-rung MEANING row.

SR-234Contested or repeated review findings receive a bounded adjudicationre-accept owed

Requirement

Where a review finding is contested by the builder or coordinator, or recurs for a third review round, the delivered adjudication content shall preserve each requested finding, the position held on it and its relevant change scope, accept only a verdict that rules every requested finding exactly once as a fix, a successor row, a reasoned dismissal in a declared class, or an escalation to the operator, and direct the dispute sitting to rule out a successor row for a fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when-gap finding.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-006 asks an unattended run to report failures clearly and surface to an operator when it cannot proceed, but it does not state who ends a contested or repeated review finding. The unattended-operations lens listens for an unbounded review loop in which the coordinator sends the same finding back to the builder without a bounded, attributable decision. A complete adjudication was chosen so an independent call can settle each requested finding without silently adding, dropping or defaulting one. Fed back to the need: SN-006's acceptance could state that contested review findings receive a bounded ruling; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-235Attended independent review verdicts are recorded or refusedre-accept owed

Requirement

When an attended launcher submits an independent review verdict for a work item's lane, the delivered review content shall record a verdict bound to the reviewed commit in the review-round record form the delivered verdict reporting reads, or refuse a malformed or unbound verdict without a record.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-024 requires an independent critical eye and assigns the attended reviewer to the operator, but does not require that verdict to survive as review history. The integrity-and-recoverability lens listens for a durable artifact updated without an all-or-nothing guarantee: accepting an unbound or malformed verdict can associate the wrong judgement with a lane, while dropping a recorded verdict leaves the next reader with no record of the independent review. A validated record-or-refusal boundary was chosen over treating submitted text as history because the latter cannot distinguish a verdict for the reviewed commit from unrelated text. Fed back to the need: SN-024's acceptance could name a durable attended-review record; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

Detail 0% of the words changed
Round accepts only a full-lane review with no prior findings or a narrow review that names the prior findings file. render_review strictly fills the shipped reviewer template with the work-item specification, lane range, scratch location, optional review rubric and verdict destination; an empty derived set is a valid round, renders no test command, and states that the row touches no code; listed evidence and reported gaps render beside the test command; render_critique strictly fills the shipped critique template with the work-item specification and named rubric. Both refuse a missing specification, unreadable or empty named input, or unfilled template slot before a brief is written. review_refusal accepts only a verdict bound to the reviewed full commit after the shared review-line reader accepts exactly one line whose keyword, in any case, is VERDICT, in exactly the canonical form `VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`, whose count matches the finding lines the review scorer reads from declared-severity brackets and whose changes request names a finding. round_path chooses the next ordinal lane round filename, file_review writes only ana acceptedrecorded verdict as that round record when the round reader reads its lane path back as that lane's scope, and lane_commits resolves commits on a branch and requires the base to be an ancestor of the reviewed commit. A first plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when alone, opens with that commit, and refuses a missing rubric, plan or specification, a missing or beyond delta, a coverage failure, or a third round. A second plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when and the first critique's finding identifiers, never their text, uses convergence stance, and refuses a revision that leaves a first-critique finding neither covered nor excluded. A single-plan brief strictly fills the shipped single-plan template with the specification, ordered Done-when clauses, required registry references, and one planner output path; a revision additionally labels the committed plan and latest filed critique findings as claims under judgement. It refuses a missing specification, Done-when, plan or critique, or an unfilled slot. A critique record is filed only when it is bound to an ancestor that holds the plan and has the verdict form; a pass record is written only from committed cited records, passing plan coverage, and a passing delta, after an approval or an accepted dismissal of every blocking and major second-round finding. At the cap, a dispute findings file is written only from the committed second critique, giving each blocking and major finding the identifier of its position among all critique findings, its text verbatim, and a declared position; it refuses another identifier set or an existing file. The second plan critique's brief never carries the first critique's verdict or any finding's text. A review round is ordinary by default or convergence: ordinary emits no stance line, while convergence emits one fixed stance line after the range and refuses a narrow scope or unknown stance before writing a brief. An ordinary review reading scope reads the delegated-decisions record and filed plan critiques, while a convergence scope excludes both; a convergence render refuses a reviewer template whose reading-scope command does not carry the review-record exclusion exactly once. The scope critique names the component and interface registries, derived architecture, runtime flows, and dependency ledger, marking an absent registry; the single-plan brief and scope critique render their registry lines from one declared set. A plan critique ties every severity class to a normal-use-reachable defect: a fail-open, data-loss, or security path counts only when a supported workflow or the kit's own routes reach it, and a rare or contrived path is MINOR at most or dismissed. Its confirming round treats a new finding as BLOCKER or MAJOR only when it is a reachable fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when gap; anything else is MINOR. A finding line bearing the convergence-class tag defined by LLR-311 is filed and counted as one finding under the unchanged verdict grammar.

SR-236Rework plans cover reviewed findingsre-accept owed

Requirement

When a reviewed change requires rework, the delivered review workflow shall dispatch that rework only after its plan covers, or excludes with a reason, every finding of the review it answers as a clause in the order written; an exclusion based on a dispute ruling resolves a finding only when an accepted dismissal or successor ruling ruled that same finding.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-024 requires an independent critical eye to drive rework, but does not say how a rework plan preserves every finding that eye raised. The unattended-operations lens listens for a green because nothing looked: dispatching from a plan that omits, renumbers or substitutes a finding lets the change appear answered while the reviewer's concern received no response. Treating every reasoned exclusion as a resolution was rejected because a disputed finding remains open unless its accepted dismissal or successor ruling decided that very finding; keeping each finding as an ordered clause makes the plan and review commensurable. Fed back to the need: SN-024's acceptance could state that rework answers every review finding.

SR-237Blackout pauses new model work and resumes it after the windowre-accept owed

Requirement

When a declared blackout window is armed, the delivered coordination and unattended operation shall pause new model work until the window ends, preserving each claimed lane at its committed pause point and starting no model work inside the window except an adjudication needed to bring an active lane to that point, then resume eligible work after the window without retaining a session whose prior use predates that window's end.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 requires a declared pause to stop claiming and drain work already in flight without double assignment. The unattended-operations lens identifies a high-usage interval as a pause that must not discard lane state, while the integrity lens identifies a stale retained transcript as an unsafe substitute for a fresh resume. Keeping the active claim and committed evidence was chosen over a second held state because it preserves the recovery model.

A new ordinary call or claim is refused during the interval; an adjudication for an active claimed work item may run to its pause point; the loop waits and retries after the interval; and the first retained keep after the interval retires a record last used before its end while a use at or after the end remains eligible to resume.

guard_config reads the declared coordinator threshold and window: a non-positive, out-of-range or malformed threshold is off and a malformed window reads as the default. read_occupancy reads the newest valid assistant usage after the live transcript branch's latest compaction boundary, never a sidechain record, counting input and cached input; a record whose usage is malformed, partial or zero is skipped, and no valid usage reads as unknown, never zero. A primary-checkout lease names one coordinator session and its transcript. take refuses another holder; release frees the lease and clear unlatches it, each requiring and recording the owner'soperator's reason; hand_back accepts only the holder session and a handoff carrying a session prompt, frees the lease, and records the handoff; it refuses another or unnamed caller, whatever handoff it names, while naming the owner'soperator's release; it refuses the holder's own pending relaunch request, while a previous holder's request does not block it and is left for session_end's foreign-request refusal; with the guard off it returns before reading or writing. Elapsed time never transfers ownership. on_session_start installs a session as holder, unlatched, only when it presents the successor token the holder's exit wrote into the lease, and restates a latched drain to the holder's own resumed start. Only the holder's own hook payload on the holder's transcript is measured, never a subagent's. latch_reading latches drain when the unrounded reading reaches the threshold and retains it through lower readings, compaction and resume; it ends only through the owner's clear, the owner'soperator's release, the holder's hand-back, or a successor take. window_refusal runs before the dial on every claim route, including the dispatcher, naming the UTC end; the dispatcher remains exempt only from the context guard. claim_refusal identifies the claimant by the session id the agent CLI exports to its tool processes (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID), refuses with no lease held or a claimant that is not the holder, and reads and latches the holder's transcript itself, so a refusal never depends on a hook having run; a claim holding the dispatch lock never calls it. While a window is armed hooks act at every dial and deny the closed list of the main session's Agent call, SendMessage call, Bash/PowerShell model-CLI command word, and a Bash/PowerShell line unreadable only because of an unclosed single quote, unclosed double quote, unclosed POSIX dollar quote, unclosed POSIX backtick substitution, unclosed dollar-parenthesis substitution, or unclosed PowerShell here-string. One quote-aware shell reading per dialect reads quoted values as the shell does, and treats quoted separators, comments and here-document and here-string bodies as data. It finds the model-CLI command word after leading variable assignments, the timeout and env prefixes, the shell's reserved words, the chain operators and the call operator, and in substitutions written in the line or inside double quotes. It reads a PowerShell assignment to a variable as running its right-hand command, while a quoted or variable right-hand value stays data. A form outside this list gets no dedicated recognition: it may incidentally match this reading, and carries no guarantee either way. window_check exits nonzero inside an armed window. At every SessionStart inside a window, hooks inject the blackout close-down instruction; each main session's monitored events inject it at that session's first monitored event in the window and every twentieth thereafter, counted per session per window: bring each open lane to its pause point, using a wrap-up adjudication for an active claim where needed; write the handoff naming each lane and its next obligation; request no relaunch; and end the session. Hook responses inject the latch instruction once and bounded reminders thereafter; inside a blackout window the latch is still recorded, but the blackout close-down, which requests no relaunch, is injected in its place. PreCompact records trigger, occupancy and latch/request state; classify_compaction reports missed-threshold, manual and during-drain cases. Before recording a holder, the lease take refuses an inactive commit floor and records no holder. After identifying a session, the lease take first reads the guard hooks' state and records no holder unless it reads none or on, or a terminal consent installs them and the re-read reads on; without a terminal at absent, or at occupied, it refuses naming the consent step or the hooks to move.

SR-238A deadline or interruption ends the session process treere-accept owed

Requirement

When a declared deadline or coordinator interruption ends a session, the delivered coordinator shall end every process in the session process group on POSIX or session job on Windows.

Rationale

A descendant can outlive the direct session child and keep editing the worktree handed to the next session. Ending only the direct child was rejected because it leaves that concurrent writer outside the coordinator's supervision. The bounded guarantee excludes a descendant that leaves the session process group and a process another service starts outside the session job: neither is ended, and the kill does not report it. A POSIX zombie under a PID 1 that never reaps keeps the group nonempty, so the kill raises after the bound. A descendant that denies the kill access to wait on it also makes the kill raise, rather than letting the coordinator continue without knowing whether it ended. Stopping is the need's cannot-proceed case, not a supervision fault: continuing would hand the worktree to the next session beside a writer that may still be live, and nothing can proceed safely past that. Two windows lie outside the guarantee, each sub-second and on no supported workflow's ordinary path: an interruption while the session is still being launched, before the coordinator supervises it, which can leave a running child; and a process that joins the session job while the kill takes its member list, which is terminated with the job but can still be ending, for milliseconds, when the coordinator continues.

AcceptanceCriteriaAt a wall deadline, an idle deadline, or a coordinator interruption while the coordinator supervises a launched session, the direct session child and every process in the session process group on POSIX, or in the session job when the kill takes its member list on Windows, have ended before the coordinator continues; a process that joins the session job later in the kill is terminated with the job; if any has not ended within 10 s of the kill, the coordinator stops with an error naming what survived instead of continuing.

Bookkeeping never raises StoreBusy: when its apply is deferred, its accounting carries reset-reason pending and the call's own session-gen. A launch that raises retires the session it resumed (keep_abandon); a first mint that raises removes its lease-only record. This is guaranteed under lock contention for every marker kind: every locked read (load_honoured, in keep_for, keep_release, keep_bookkeep, keep_abandon, retire_scope and take_warm_lease) reads the clock first, then lists and folds the record's markers in publication order, then runs retire_stale_lease, so no reader retires a lease whose release was published before it observed expiry. A release drops its publisher's lease; a retire retires only the live session and generation it names and drops a lease only when its publisher holds it; a bookkeep lands under _landing's rule, and one that no longer lands releases its holder's lease if still held. Every marker therefore takes effect at most once: a call's marker only while its publisher's lease stands, and a scope retirement only on the live session and generation it names, so a marker left by a failed delete is inert on a later locked or lockless read. A lease-only record without a lease is removed. Each applied or spent marker is deleted by its own name, never another's; an unreadable marker stays and prevents expiry retirement on that read, while a malformed marker is deleted with one stderr line. The lockless readers (due_routes, _warm_candidates, scoped_route and _scoped_records) fold the same markers without deleting them: a pending bookkeep or release remains eligible for warm handling, while a pending retire is neither due nor pinned. KEEP-WARM (KeepWarmer, built by keep_warmer when keepwarm_minutes is also on, ticked once per dispatcher poll by run): keepwarm_due is true for an ANTHROPIC active session idle keepwarm_minutes while lanes are out, and a ping is taken only on a route whose runner's adapter bounds a call to one turn (claude's), so a route served through any other runner is never pinged; take_warm_lease prepares the selected route under the lock before any lease; a preparation refusal, or a prepared family differing from the record family, skips without a lease, otherwise the warmed Keep carries that Prepared family and home. The ping (role KEEP-WARM, source keep-warm, prompt ack, bounded by one_turn to --max-turns 1, a 300 s wall) runs on its own thread through act, so the tick never waits; one ping at a time, a due ping while one is in flight skipped and said; its session log is written to the primary-checkout spool, never committed, by the dispatcher's own thread between polls only over a clean trunk, else held and said; at the run's end a ping in flight is waited out and recorded to that spool by the same clean-trunk rule, and over a dirty trunk its log is not written and the reason is printed and returned. A ping whose launch raised TreeNotEnded hands it with the finished call to the dispatcher's thread, and the tick that sees it, or the run's end, raises it: over a clean trunk after recording the call, a failure to record riding as its context; over a dirty trunk unrecorded, the hold not deferring it. Any other failure of the ping is recorded as an ERROR call and the run continues. REVIEW. reviewer_dials is the one reader of the reviewer table: it reads a 0..100 non-boolean integer reset percent and persisted final reviewer only while that percent is positive; absent, unreadable, unparseable or ill-typed settings read as off and fresh. review_retention returns ReviewRetention(scope, stage, pin): it returns no scope for a non-review phase, no claim base, or an off review dial; a narrow round uses the iteration stage; a full round retires live iteration records through retire markers, which take effect for the lockless pin at once and are applied by the next locked read, and is unretained when fresh or uses the final stage when persisted. scoped_route pins a live record after folding its pending markers for the settled scope; unavailable pins fall through ordinary selection. Scoped records skip same-artifact reset, drain at the review percent, are clear at every round, and are never keep-warm due. _read_record is the one reader for load and scans: it accepts only writer-produced lease-only, retired-first, or full variants with all consumed fields typed and each optional occupancy, use or compaction field of its writer's type, filed under _record_name; any other object, absent or unreadable file is no record and the call mints. The loop stores scope, stage and once-resolved review template content in routing state, and passes scope and that content only for a review keep.
Rationale 0% of the words changed
Retention is one more thing a call does, not a second launch path, so resume, occupancy, reset and keep-warm all go through act and record, and the rules and the store sit in their own module beside the service rather than in the roles. The layer ships off because turning it on is the owner'soperator's decision after it has been verified on the machine it runs on, and at the off dial the launch is exactly a fresh session's. The lock and the lease exist because a lane's worker and the dispatcher both reach the one store and the one transcript: a torn record or two calls resuming one session at once corrupts the state every later judgement reads. The clear point reads the queue and the lanes rather than the item alone because a draining session that retires while a successor of its own verdict is still queued breaks the round trip the layer exists for. The keep-warm ping is off the dispatcher's thread so a slow ping cannot stall the merges, and its record is on it so its commit is serialised with them. A qualified account home keeps its retained transcript out of a person's own sessions, while an unqualified entry retains in its ambient launch environment; a long-lived credential is read only for the launch that needs it, so no retained record becomes a credential store. The review class uses the existing store, lease and service homes rather than a copy; scoped identity keeps its records distinct from adjudicator records and preserves empty-scope filenames.

SR-239Where the reviewer retention dial is on, loop review routes retain only their scoped reviewer sessionsre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop review content shall, if the reviewer setting is malformed, or names a persisted final reviewer while retention is off, read it as retention off and a fresh final reviewer; otherwise, where the declared reviewer retention dial is above zero, resume a reviewer only across iteration rounds for one lane, claim and review phase, keyed by those values and the iteration stage; read an absent, unreadable, malformed, misfiled or differently keyed retained record as no session and start fresh; never keep a reviewer session warm; retire that iteration session when the lane's full-lane round is drawn; run that round fresh, or, where the declared final-reviewer setting selects persistence, on one retained final reviewer per lane and phase that never resumes an iteration session; treat a change to the template a retained reviewer's brief is built from as a change of its governing inputs; and record session-mode and keep-scope as audit-only columns.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement. The Performance, Unattended Operations and Integrity Recoverability lenses identify the operating cost, unattended judgement degradation, and shared-state corruption risk of repeatedly minting reviewer sessions. Repeated fresh reviewer rounds can exhaust the available plan, while scoped identity prevents one lane or review stage from inheriting another transcript. Coordinator-written review-scope and session-generation records, not reviewer-authored text, establish final-review provenance; session-mode and keep-scope remain audit-only. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name bounded operating cost per reviewer judgement as part of what lets a run proceed with no human curating it; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SN-RefsSN-025
Boundary-RefsB-10
Hat-RefsPERFORMANCE;UNATTENDED-OPS;INTEGRITY-RECOVERABILITY
AcceptanceCriteriaWith the reviewer dial at zero, every review round launches fresh. With it on, two iteration rounds of one lane and phase resume one session while another lane starts its own; a record under another keying, an undeclared record shape, or a record filed under another key reads as no session; drawing the lane's full-lane round retires its iteration session; with a fresh final reviewer the full-lane round is fresh, and with a persisted one it resumes only the final reviewer's own session. A malformed reviewer setting, or a persisted final reviewer while retention is off, reads as retention off and fresh. Gate admission is specified by SR-156. Each review session log records session-mode and keep-scope as audit-only columns.

This is guaranteed under lock contention for every marker kind: every locked read (load_honoured, in keep_for, keep_release, keep_bookkeep, keep_abandon, retire_scope and take_warm_lease) reads the clock first, then lists and folds the record's markers in publication order, then runs retire_stale_lease, so no reader retires a lease whose release was published before it observed expiry. A release drops its publisher's lease; a retire retires only the live session and generation it names and drops a lease only when its publisher holds it; a bookkeep lands under _landing's rule, and one that no longer lands releases its holder's lease if still held. Every marker therefore takes effect at most once: a call's marker only while its publisher's lease stands, and a scope retirement only on the live session and generation it names, so a marker left by a failed delete is inert on a later locked or lockless read. A lease-only record without a lease is removed. Each applied or spent marker is deleted by its own name, never another's; an unreadable marker stays and prevents expiry retirement on that read, while a malformed marker is deleted with one stderr line. The lockless readers (due_routes, _warm_candidates, scoped_route and _scoped_records) fold the same markers without deleting them: a pending bookkeep or release remains eligible for warm handling, while a pending retire is neither due nor pinned. KEEP-WARM (KeepWarmer, built by keep_warmer when keepwarm_minutes is also on, ticked once per dispatcher poll by run): keepwarm_due is true for an ANTHROPIC active session idle keepwarm_minutes while lanes are out, and a ping is taken only on a route whose runner's adapter bounds a call to one turn (claude's), so a route served through any other runner is never pinged; take_warm_lease prepares the selected route under the lock before any lease; a preparation refusal, or a prepared family differing from the record family, skips without a lease, otherwise the warmed Keep carries that Prepared family and home. The ping (role KEEP-WARM, source keep-warm, prompt ack, bounded by one_turn to --max-turns 1, a 300 s wall) runs on its own thread through act, so the tick never waits; one ping at a time, a due ping while one is in flight skipped and said; its session log is written to the primary-checkout spool, never committed, by the dispatcher's own thread between polls only over a clean trunk, else held and said; at the run's end a ping in flight is waited out and recorded to that spool by the same clean-trunk rule, and over a dirty trunk its log is not written and the reason is printed and returned. A ping whose launch raised TreeNotEnded hands it with the finished call to the dispatcher's thread, and the tick that sees it, or the run's end, raises it: over a clean trunk after recording the call, a failure to record riding as its context; over a dirty trunk unrecorded, the hold not deferring it. Any other failure of the ping is recorded as an ERROR call and the run continues. REVIEW. reviewer_dials is the one reader of the reviewer table: it reads a 0..100 non-boolean integer reset percent and persisted final reviewer only while that percent is positive; absent, unreadable, unparseable or ill-typed settings read as off and fresh. review_retention returns ReviewRetention(scope, stage, pin): it returns no scope for a non-review phase, no claim base, or an off review dial; a narrow round uses the iteration stage; a full round retires live iteration records through retire markers, which take effect for the lockless pin at once and are applied by the next locked read, and is unretained when fresh or uses the final stage when persisted. scoped_route pins a live record after folding its pending markers for the settled scope; unavailable pins fall through ordinary selection. Scoped records skip same-artifact reset, drain at the review percent, are clear at every round, and are never keep-warm due. _read_record is the one reader for load and scans: it accepts only writer-produced lease-only, retired-first, or full variants with all consumed fields typed and each optional occupancy, use or compaction field of its writer's type, filed under _record_name; any other object, absent or unreadable file is no record and the call mints. The loop stores scope, stage and once-resolved review template content in routing state, and passes scope and that content only for a review keep.
Rationale 0% of the words changed
Retention is one more thing a call does, not a second launch path, so resume, occupancy, reset and keep-warm all go through act and record, and the rules and the store sit in their own module beside the service rather than in the roles. The layer ships off because turning it on is the owner'soperator's decision after it has been verified on the machine it runs on, and at the off dial the launch is exactly a fresh session's. The lock and the lease exist because a lane's worker and the dispatcher both reach the one store and the one transcript: a torn record or two calls resuming one session at once corrupts the state every later judgement reads. The clear point reads the queue and the lanes rather than the item alone because a draining session that retires while a successor of its own verdict is still queued breaks the round trip the layer exists for. The keep-warm ping is off the dispatcher's thread so a slow ping cannot stall the merges, and its record is on it so its commit is serialised with them. A qualified account home keeps its retained transcript out of a person's own sessions, while an unqualified entry retains in its ambient launch environment; a long-lived credential is read only for the launch that needs it, so no retained record becomes a credential store. The review class uses the existing store, lease and service homes rather than a copy; scoped identity keeps its records distinct from adjudicator records and preserves empty-scope filenames.

SR-242A capped sequence of red review bars closes partialre-accept owed

Requirement

When an unattended lane reaches its declared maximum number of consecutive red review-bar rounds, the delivered dispatcher shall close the lane partial and report that cap outcome separately.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement through the PERFORMANCE lens: SN-004 and SN-008 require trustworthy, fail-closed outcomes, but leave an unattended lane free to spend unbounded rounds on a known red condition. A declared finite cap was selected over an implicit iteration limit because the outcome must remain attributable to repeated review-bar failure and recoverable from committed evidence. Fed back to the needs: their acceptance could state that a red review-bar rebuild sequence ends in a partial close at its declared cap rather than consuming unbounded review rounds or escalating through the approval level.

SR-244Transcript-derived usage records include coordinated nested agentsre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordination capability shall record once each transcript-bearing model session that coordination completion ingests for coordinated work, including every session an agent spawns at any nesting depth, with its identity and transcript-derived usage; record no already-recorded message, duplicate no service record, grant its record no gate authority, include no transcript text, refuse an unknown source shape, and direct completion to ingest the current session and a named prior-session tail.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement through the PERFORMANCE lens: SN-026 makes model-family routing a configurable operating choice, but does not require the cost of coordinated sessions outside the launcher result to be visible. The lens identifies an incomplete cost reading when nested work is omitted or a repeated or resumed read inflates it. Recorded probes establish that a resume appends to its existing transcript, that a Claude result excludes sub-agent usage, and that arbitrary nesting occurs; a sub-agent's final hand-back often has no stop record and is complete once the session's transcripts show the agent finished. The direct-child fan-out re-stamp is intentional: the independently observable reader, identity, contribution, recovery, duplication, shape, source-selection, record, CLI, and completion decisions must not be merged. Fed back to the need: its acceptance could require the operator to see complete, non-duplicated usage for coordinated work across the configured families.

SR-247An earlier kit's stored values reach the current vocabulary through a migratorapproval owed

Requirement

The delivered kit shall provide a migrator that rewrites, in place, the stored values an earlier kit vocabulary spelled differently and a current script still reads, and that changes nothing else in a file it rewrites.

Rationale

The kit's vocabulary was unified so that one word names one thing, and the operator ruled out readers of an earlier spelling in the core scripts. A repository that still stores one would then read as if the value were absent, so a purpose-built migrator is the path from an earlier kit and the one place the earlier spellings are known. It rewrites whole values in known places and proves each rewrite by parsing the file again, because a migration that guessed inside prose, or changed a cell it was not asked to change, would alter a record nobody reviewed.

SR SR-247changed, Drafted — never approved
AcceptanceCriteria 30% of the words changed
Run over a repository that stores earlier spellings, the migrator rewrites each value it names where that value is stored: the outcome of a verdict binding; a registry's field name and that field's value under either carrier, in the live registry and in the acceptance record's copy of it; and a table, a key andkey, a value and an element of a list in the policy file.file; and the verdict key of each entry in a delegated-decisions record. Every other byte of a rewritten file is unchanged, its line endings included. A file whose rewrite would parse as anything other than the named change is left untouched, is named in the output, and makes the run exit 1. It renames the operator's scratchpad from its earlier file name without reading it, and a scratchpad present under both names is left as it is, is named, and makes the run exit 1. With --check nothing is written and the run exits 1 when a rewrite is owed. A second run finds nothing to do and exits 0.

Detail
migrate_vocabulary.py imports nothing from the kit. STEPS names each step and main runs them in order, printing one line per rewritten file, per file that owes the rewrite under --check, and per file left untouched; it exits 1 when a file could not be rewritten safely, or under --check when a rewrite is owed. bindings rewrites the line outcome = accepted to outcome = recorded in each .requested file under docs/reviews through _rewrite, which keeps every byte outside the match. registry_paths yields each .toml and .csv file directly under docs/requirements and docs/test, then the same files under either name of the acceptance record's directory. FIELDS maps an earlier field name to the current one per carrier and VALUES maps an earlier value to the current one within a field; _current applies both to one cell, matching the value on its stripped text and keeping its padding. migrate_toml rewrites one-line quoted cells with _toml_cell and returns the text only when its parse equals _toml_expected, the parse of the original with each row's fields and values moved; a row carrying both spellings of a field, a file that does not parse and any other difference raise Unsafe. migrate_csv keeps a byte-order mark and the leading run of blank and comment lines that _csv_preamble measures, the preamble the kit's CSV reader drops, then reads cell spans after it with _csv_records, which folds doubled quotes through _csv_quoted and ends a bare cell through _csv_bare; _csv_edits replaces the h… [2472 more chars — read the registry row]
Rationale
A whole value in a known place is the only thing a migrator can move without judging prose, and a second parse is what proves that nothing else moved: a look-alike line inside a multi-line cell changes the parse and so refuses the file. Spans keep quoting, padding, comments and line endings, so the diff a repository commits is the vocabulary and nothing else. Importing nothing from the kit lets the migrator run while the kit's own scripts cannot yet read the repository.

SN-006DRIFTED

Acceptance 3% of the words changed
The unattended loop resumes from the repository's tracked status surface, exits a **typed code** at each end state, and a preflight refuses a broken footing (no agent CLI, not a git repo, private author under privacy-check) rather than hanging. During unattended operation, configured limits bound every spawned worker and irreversible action, and only an explicit human-providedoperator-provided override may exceed those limits. A fault in a limit's own enforcement is recorded and lets the run continue rather than halting it — the run surfaces to aan humanoperator when it cannot proceed, never when its own supervision errs.
Need 3% of the words changed
An agent can run **unattended** and resume from repository text alone. Such a run never waits for interactive input, and reports its failures clearly. It also stays **safe**: declared limits bound the workers it may set running and the actions it takes that cannot be undone, and only an override aan humanoperator provides — never one the model can set — may relax those limits. That safety is **supervision rather than an absolute**: the layer's first obligation is to move forward as far as it can, and it surfaces to aan humanoperator when it cannot proceed — so a fault in the machinery that carries a limit degrades to a recorded condition, not to a stopped run.

Tagsunattended;loop;legal;personal-data
WhyOne family is a single point of both failure and bias: an outage, a retired model or an expired auth stalls the whole loop, and a reviewer drawn from the implementer's own family shares its blind spots — so a same-family review reads like corroboration while adding little. Declaring the families and levels in a registry, rather than hard-coding one vendor, is also what keeps the kit vendor-neutral as models turn over.
PriorityS
AcceptanceA declared agent roster carries (family × model × tier) pair-rows and a separate consent surface, whose presence turns managed selection on. The coordinator resolves a row per in-process phase and tier, prefers a cross-family draw for the reviewer, critic and planner-pair sessions, degrades to the *documented* same-family mode when only one family is routable rather than silently skipping the second opinion, and logs every selection before launch — never a silent model swap.

SN-028DRIFTED

Need 3% of the words changed
The repo owneroperator can find and change every policy dial in **one home** — a **single hand-edited, machine-read file** — and a repo that declares the same dial twice is REFUSED rather than resolved by precedence.
Why 2% of the words changed
The dials had accreted into ~10 one-word files under `docs/`, an idiom that was never ruled. Scattering costs an owneroperator one file per question and a reader five ad-hoc parsers; worse, two sources for one dial can give enforcers different policy values, and a precedence rule makes that disagreement invisible instead of loud.

SN-IDSN-028
StatusApproved
Stakeholder-RefsSTK-01
Tagsshell
PriorityS
AcceptanceA single declared process-dial file holds every process dial. Every reader obtains its policy answer from the file's TOML parse. A legacy one-word file still present alongside its key is a REFUSAL naming both, and a declared migration action — run by bootstrap and by the documented re-sync — converts and deletes each legacy file it can confirm in the policy declaration and, when it cannot write one, leaves it intact with a named refusal and hand-edit path so an adopter never meets that refusal unaided. A wrong-typed or out-of-range dial is refused, never defaulted.

SN-029DRIFTED

Acceptance 4% of the words changed
A cumulative level names the highest tier aan humanoperator still approves, compared against a separately derived SPINE STAGE (which tier is in process) via a declared, auditable mapping. Every failure direction — an unreadable stage, an out-of-range level, a wrong-typed dial — resolves toward MORE humanoperator involvement, because the failure that matters is a machine approving something aan humanoperator meant to hold. Each acceptance is anchored ON THE ACCEPTED ARTIFACT'S OWN ROW — the commit whose tree carries the accepted text, plus a digest of that row's normative cells — never in a second registry keyed on the same artifact. Text that has moved away from what was accepted surfaces regardless of any Status movement, the one signal the sanctioned amend-and-flip path would otherwise hide, so an AMENDED requirement drops the derived stage exactly as a newly introduced one does. Each automated approval on a released tier appends a durable record (row, transition, acting reviewer, commit) distinguishable from aan humanoperator approval by query.
Need 4% of the words changed
**An autonomous run gets as far as it honestly can.** Once triggered, the coordinator stops for aan humanoperator judgement only when the declared approval level reserves that tier for aan human,operator, when a round cannot converge on its own, or when requirement/test documentation is introduced or amended such that the gate drops below what automation is permitted to attest. On every tier released to automation, an approval still happens as a review from a declared perspective against the row's actual evidence, and leaves a record naming who or what approved it — releasing a tier means the review is delegated, never skipped.
Why 2% of the words changed
The unattended layer only pays for itself if a walk-away run actually walks away — so what stops it must be exactly the set of judgements the owneroperator reserved, and nothing else. A three-value gate-authority enum (`attended` / `single-approve` / `autonomous`) cannot express "TCs are human-heldoperator-held but LLRs are not", the distinction an owneroperator actually wants to dial, and leaves each consuming table free to re-interpret the same word with its own fail-safe direction. Answering "has this been approved?" by walking git for the newest commit where a row reads `Verified` is sound only while every amendment flips its row in the same commit — precisely the sanctioned path an amendment detector ignores — so the blessed way to amend an attested requirement is invisible to every consumer, and a stakeholder need has no anchor at all (an SN has no Status cell).
